title: Polynomial-time planted-clique detection below the square-root scale
open: Determine whether a randomized polynomial-time algorithm can distinguish \(G(n,1/2)\) from the same graph with a planted clique of size \(\lfloor n^{1/3}\rfloor\), with error tending to zero.
status: A longstanding average-case complexity problem. Exhaustive search succeeds well below the regime reached by standard polynomial-time methods; planted-clique assumptions support numerous conditional statistical lower bounds.
why: A resolution would change computational feasibility claims across high-dimensional statistics.
key_works: Berthet and Rigollet, 2013, “Complexity Theoretic Lower Bounds for Sparse Principal Component Detection,” PMLR 30; Brennan, Bresler, and Huleihel, 2018, “Reducibility and Computational Lower Bounds for Problems with Planted Sparse Structure,” arXiv:1806.07508.

title: Complete computational minimax frontier for sparse PCA
open: Characterize the best polynomial-time estimation risk for a sparse leading eigenvector across sample size, ambient dimension, sparsity, and signal strength, including transition regimes rather than only separated asymptotic cases.
status: Information-theoretic rates, efficient algorithms, and conditional hardness results cover substantial regions. A single sharp computational risk characterization, including boundary behavior and constants, remains a research target.
why: It would identify when additional data can substitute for unavailable computation.
key_works: Berthet and Rigollet, 2013, “Complexity Theoretic Lower Bounds for Sparse Principal Component Detection”; Brennan, Bresler, and Huleihel, 2018, “Reducibility and Computational Lower Bounds for Problems with Planted Sparse Structure,” arXiv:1806.07508.

title: Tensor PCA below known efficient thresholds
open: For a rank-one order-three tensor in Gaussian noise, determine the smallest signal allowing polynomial-time weak recovery, and whether the information–computation gap is intrinsic.
status: The gap has been studied since at least 2014. Information-theoretic recovery and available algorithmic guarantees operate at different signal scales; computational conclusions depend on the algorithm class or hardness hypothesis.
why: It would clarify the limits of higher-order latent-variable estimation.
key_works: Montanari and Richard, 2014, “A statistical model for tensor PCA,” arXiv:1411.1076.

title: Hypergraphic planted-clique hardness
open: Establish credible average-case hardness results for detecting planted cliques in uniform hypergraphs, including reductions that preserve the statistically relevant signal and size regimes.
status: Explicitly posed as an open problem in 2020. Graph planted-clique hardness does not automatically transfer with the desired parameters to every hypergraphic model.
why: It would support or overturn computational barriers claimed for tensor and higher-order network inference.
key_works: Luo and Zhang, 2020, “Open problem: average-case hardness of hypergraphic planted clique detection,” COLT, pp. 3852–3856; Maleki et al., 2026, “High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems,” arXiv:2605.05076.

title: Submatrix detection with uncertain heterogeneous noise
open: Derive matching statistical and computational detection boundaries for an unknown elevated-mean rectangle when entry variances are heterogeneous and estimated from limited auxiliary observations.
status: Research target extending the established homogeneous submatrix model. Classical computational barriers do not by themselves characterize the interaction between variance-estimation error, rectangular sparsity, and signal strength.
why: It would make biclustering guarantees relevant to unevenly measured biological and industrial data.
key_works: Ma and Wu, 2015, “Computational barriers in minimax submatrix detection,” arXiv:1309.5914, DOI:10.1214/14-AOS1300.

title: Corrected low-degree principles for statistical computation
open: Identify explicit model classes and regularity conditions under which low-degree polynomial performance reliably predicts the capabilities of broader polynomial-time or quasipolynomial-time algorithms.
status: The unrestricted quasipolynomial low-degree conjecture was disproved in 2025. The open task is a defensible replacement, not proving that false formulation.
why: It would turn a widely used computational heuristic into a precisely scoped theory.
key_works: Buhai, Hsieh, Jain, and Kothari, 2025, “The Quasi-Polynomial Low-Degree Conjecture is False,” arXiv:2505.17360.

title: Inference with dense unknown precision matrices
open: Characterize covariance classes permitting honest, computationally efficient confidence intervals for sparse-regression coefficients when the inverse design covariance is dense and cannot be consistently estimated entrywise.
status: Debiasing methods work under several structural regimes. The outstanding issue is the attainable frontier beyond familiar sparsity or strong covariance restrictions, not whether debiasing ever works.
why: It would broaden trustworthy inference for strongly correlated predictors.
key_works: Maleki et al., 2026, “High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems,” arXiv:2605.05076.

title: Universality for correlated non-Gaussian designs
open: Find verifiable dependence conditions under which precise high-dimensional risk formulas remain universal when design entries are correlated and non-Gaussian.
status: Universality is established for important independent-entry settings; arbitrary isotropic designs admit counterexamples. The open problem is a useful intermediate class with sharp assumptions.
why: It would justify Gaussian-derived predictions for realistic structured data.
key_works: Han and Shen, 2023, “Universality of regularized regression estimators in high dimensions,” arXiv:2206.07936, DOI:10.1214/23-AOS2309.

title: Exact asymptotics with dependence across every design entry
open: Obtain tractable limiting risks and fluctuation laws for regularized estimators under matrix-valued Gaussian designs such as \(X=\sum_i g_iA_i\), where deterministic matrices induce general entrywise dependence.
status: Explicit research direction in the 2026 high-dimensional statistics survey. Independent-row or separable-covariance results do not cover the full matrix-series setting.
why: It would connect precise statistical theory to structured sensing and repeated-measurement systems.
key_works: Maleki et al., 2026, “High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems,” arXiv:2605.05076.

title: Confidence sets through eigenvalue collisions
open: Construct honest confidence sets that adapt between identifiable individual eigenvectors and only-identifiable invariant subspaces as population eigengaps shrink at unknown rates.
status: Spectral-projector normal approximations provide a substantial baseline. Uniform inference across merging eigenvalues requires handling a changing identifiable parameter.
why: It would prevent falsely precise principal-component interpretations near degeneracy.
key_works: Koltchinskii and Lounici, 2017, “Normal approximation and concentration of spectral projectors of sample covariance,” arXiv:1504.07333, DOI:10.1214/16-AOS1437.

title: Shared-subspace uncertainty with partially paired modalities
open: Develop confidence sets for shared and modality-specific subspaces when subjects are only partially paired, ranks are selected from data, and pairing probabilities depend on observed covariates.
status: JIVE and probabilistic extensions already exist, including ProJIVE in 2026. The target is joint uncertainty accounting for missing pairing and rank selection, not another decomposition algorithm.
why: It would make multimodal integration interpretable beyond point estimates.
key_works: Lock et al., 2013, “Joint and individual variation explained (JIVE) for integrated analysis of multiple data types,” arXiv:1102.4110; Murden et al., 2026, “Probabilistic Joint and Individual Variation Explained (ProJIVE) for Data Integration,” arXiv:2603.12351.

title: Logistic-regression inference near the separation transition
open: Derive finite-size scaling laws and uniformly valid inference when high-dimensional logistic regression approaches the boundary between existence and nonexistence of the maximum-likelihood estimator.
status: Modern proportional-asymptotic theory describes major departures from classical likelihood theory. The critical window and practical uncertainty statements across it remain a sharper target.
why: It would identify when familiar coefficient estimates become fundamentally unstable.
key_works: Sur and Candès, 2019, “A modern maximum-likelihood theory for high-dimensional logistic regression,” arXiv:1803.06964, DOI:10.1073/pnas.1810420116.

title: Log-free resilient cores under covariance bounds
open: Determine whether \(O(d/\epsilon)\) samples from every mean-zero distribution with covariance bounded by the identity contain a \((1-\epsilon)\)-fraction subset with universally bounded empirical second moment, with constant high probability.
status: Explicitly listed in a 2025 robust-statistics open-problem lecture; the comparison bound includes an additional logarithmic dimension factor.
why: It would sharpen the sample foundations of robust estimation.
key_works: University of Washington CSE 599K, 2025, “Lecture 18: Some open problems in robust statistics (and friends),” December 1.

title: Standard-assumption hardness for bounded-moment robust means
open: Establish computational lower bounds, under broadly accepted assumptions, separating information-theoretic robust mean rates under bounded fourth or higher directional moments from polynomial-time achievable rates.
status: Hardness results and algorithms depend strongly on whether moment conditions are merely true or efficiently certifiable. The distinction remains central in the 2025 open-problem discussion.
why: It would explain whether weaker modeling assumptions necessarily cost computational efficiency.
key_works: Hopkins and Li, 2019, “How hard is robust mean estimation?” arXiv:1903.07870; UW CSE 599K, 2025, “Lecture 18.”

title: The sparse robust-mean sample gap
open: Close the gap between information-theoretic and polynomial-time sample requirements for estimating a sparse mean under adversarial contamination, or prove a sharp computational barrier.
status: Efficient methods can require substantially worse sparsity dependence than unrestricted estimators. Ordinary sparse estimation and ordinary robust estimation do not settle their combination.
why: It would support reliable feature discovery in contaminated high-dimensional data.
key_works: Georgiev and Hopkins, 2022, “Privacy Induces Robustness: Information-Computation Gaps and Sparse Mean Estimation,” arXiv:2211.00724; Hopkins and Li, 2019, “How hard is robust mean estimation?”

title: Simultaneous graph inference under cellwise contamination
open: Construct simultaneous confidence statements for a sparse precision matrix when individual cells, rather than entire observations, are corrupted and contamination rates vary across coordinates.
status: Robust precision-matrix estimation under cellwise contamination has a 2015 baseline. Selection-valid edge inference and sharp uncertainty under heterogeneous contamination are stronger targets.
why: It would make corrupted laboratory and sensor tables usable for network discovery.
key_works: Loh and Tan, 2015, “High-dimensional robust precision matrix estimation: Cellwise corruption under ε-contamination,” arXiv:1509.07229.

title: Robust covariance inference with heavy tails and dependence
open: Obtain sharp confidence regions for covariance functionals under simultaneous heavy tails, temporal dependence, and a bounded fraction of adversarially corrupted observations.
status: Robust mean and covariance methods address important subsets of these difficulties. The proposed target requires an explicit joint moment–mixing–contamination class and matching lower bounds.
why: It would improve uncertainty estimates for operational and financial sensor streams.
key_works: Hopkins, Li, and Zhang, 2020, “Robust and Heavy-Tailed Mean Estimation Made Simple, via Regret Minimization,” arXiv:2007.15839; Loh, 2015, “Statistical consistency and asymptotic normality for high-dimensional robust M-estimators,” arXiv:1501.00312.

title: Streaming robust estimation with optimal memory
open: Characterize the memory–passes–risk frontier for robust sparse mean estimation when data arrive once and the adversary can adapt to previously emitted estimates.
status: Proposed theoretical and engineering target extending batch robust estimators. A meaningful solution must count memory, communication, adversarial adaptivity, and statistical error together.
why: It would enable defensible on-device and high-throughput robust analytics.
key_works: Hopkins, Li, and Zhang, 2020, “Robust and Heavy-Tailed Mean Estimation Made Simple, via Regret Minimization,” arXiv:2007.15839.

title: Adaptive bands with unknown anisotropic self-similarity
open: Construct honest, rate-adaptive confidence bands for anisotropic functions when smoothness differs by coordinate and the constants controlling self-similarity are unknown.
status: Honest adaptation is impossible over unrestricted nested smoothness classes; self-similarity permits positive results. The target is the sharp attainable anisotropic and locally varying extension.
why: It would permit uncertainty bands that adapt without hiding uncheckable tuning choices.
key_works: Bull, 2012, “Honest adaptive confidence bands and self-similar functions,” arXiv:1110.4985, DOI:10.1214/12-EJS720.

title: Confidence sets adapting to intrinsic dimension
open: Determine which separation and geometric conditions permit confidence sets to adapt simultaneously to unknown smoothness, manifold dimension, and support geometry.
status: Adaptation results exist for fixed-dimensional function and distribution classes. Unknown geometry introduces additional indistinguishability boundaries that require explicit treatment.
why: It would justify dimension-adaptive uncertainty rather than only dimension-adaptive prediction.
key_works: Deo and Randrianarisoa, 2021, “On Adaptive Confidence Sets for the Wasserstein Distances,” arXiv:2111.08505; Bull, 2012, “Honest adaptive confidence bands and self-similar functions.”

title: Adaptive conditional-independence testing
open: Derive minimax testing rates and adaptive procedures for conditional independence over classes with unknown smoothness, sparse relevant conditioning variables, and explicitly bounded conditional densities.
status: Unrestricted conditional-independence testing has strong impossibility results. The open task is to identify sharp, useful restricted classes and the cost of adapting among them.
why: It would strengthen causal discovery and conditional association screening.
key_works: Shah and Peters, 2020, “The Hardness of Conditional Independence Testing and the Generalised Covariance Measure,” arXiv:1804.07203, DOI:10.1214/19-AOS1857.

title: Power-optimal testing after learning the test representation
open: Design two-sample tests that learn kernels or representations from the tested observations while retaining finite-sample error control and near-oracle power over specified alternative classes.
status: Sample splitting and adaptive-data-analysis techniques provide valid approaches. The sharper target is the best achievable power–reuse tradeoff, rather than validity alone.
why: It would reduce the substantial power losses caused by reserving data for representation learning.
key_works: Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis,” arXiv:1411.2664; Wasserman, Ramdas, and Balakrishnan, 2020, “Universal Inference,” arXiv:1912.11436.

title: Entropy-rate estimation with unknown memory and mixing
open: Determine minimax rates for entropy-rate estimation when the process has unknown finite memory and unknown mixing strength, with procedures adapting to both.
status: Sharp results exist for important stationary reversible Markov-chain classes. Unknown memory, growing state spaces, and adaptation across mixing regimes are a distinct extension.
why: It would improve principled complexity measurement for language, biological sequences, and telemetry.
key_works: Han, Jiao, Lee, Weissman, Wu, and Yu, 2018, “Entropy Rate Estimation for Markov Chains with Large State Space,” arXiv:1802.07889.

title: Unseen-species prediction under adaptive sampling
open: Predict the number or probability mass of previously unseen species when sampling locations or collection methods are adaptively changed, and observation probabilities are only partially known.
status: Optimal extrapolation is established for several classical abundance and incidence models. Adaptive collection changes the sampling law and the estimand.
why: It would improve biodiversity surveys, rare-event discovery, and deduplication planning.
key_works: Orlitsky, Suresh, and Wu, 2016, “Optimal prediction of the number of unseen species,” DOI:10.1073/pnas.1607774113.

title: Dynamic log-concave maximum-likelihood estimation
open: Develop algorithms that update a multivariate log-concave maximum-likelihood estimate after observations are inserted or removed, with controlled approximation error and provably sub-recomputation cost.
status: Explicit computational direction in the 2025–2026 shape-constrained inference survey; improved batch computation does not settle dynamic complexity.
why: It would make shape-constrained density estimation practical for changing datasets.
key_works: Samworth, 2025/2026, “Nonparametric inference under shape constraints: past, present and future,” arXiv:2509.26040; Chen, Mazumder, and Samworth, 2024, “A new computational framework for log-concave density estimation,” DOI:10.1007/s12532-024-00252-0.

title: Log-concave estimation from partial coordinates
open: Establish identifiability, optimal rates, and feasible estimators for multivariate log-concave distributions observed through heterogeneous subsets of coordinates.
status: Identified as a future direction in the recent shape-constrained survey. Full-data rates and generic imputation do not characterize information lost through coordinate patterns.
why: It would provide distributional estimation without imposing a convenient parametric missing-data model.
key_works: Samworth, 2025/2026, “Nonparametric inference under shape constraints: past, present and future,” arXiv:2509.26040.

title: Sharp risk of smoothed log-concave estimators
open: Determine sharp global and local risk guarantees for smoothed log-concave maximum-likelihood estimators, including whether smoothing preserves optimal adaptation to simpler densities.
status: Smoothed estimators have existed since at least 2013. Their practical usefulness is ahead of a complete sharp risk theory.
why: It would justify smooth density and tail estimates rather than treating smoothing as a cosmetic step.
key_works: Chen and Samworth, 2013, “Smoothed log-concave maximum likelihood estimation with applications,” arXiv:1102.1191, DOI:10.5705/ss.2011.224.

title: Multivariate log-concave boundary limit laws
open: Derive local limiting distributions near unknown support boundaries, accounting for curvature, flat faces, and nonsmooth intersections.
status: Univariate and global theories provide starting points; multivariate boundary behavior remains substantially less developed than interior estimation.
why: It would enable calibrated uncertainty about feasible regions and extreme contours.
key_works: Groeneboom and Jongbloed, 2014, *Nonparametric Estimation under Shape Constraints*, DOI:10.1017/CBO9781139020893; Samworth, 2025/2026, “Nonparametric inference under shape constraints.”

title: Remaining logarithmic gaps in log-concave density risk
open: Remove unnecessary logarithmic factors, or prove their necessity, in global Hellinger-risk bounds for multivariate log-concave maximum-likelihood estimation.
status: Dimension-dependent polynomial rates are known. The recent survey identifies remaining logarithmic discrepancies rather than an absence of minimax theory.
why: It would complete one of shape-constrained statistics’ central benchmark problems.
key_works: Kim and Samworth, 2016, “Global rates of convergence in log-concave density estimation,” arXiv:1404.2298, DOI:10.1214/16-AOS1480.

title: Critical-moment rates under log-concave misspecification
open: Resolve the remaining rate gap for estimation of a log-concave projection at critical moment assumptions, particularly the second-moment boundary.
status: Continuity theory and convergence bounds exist; the recent survey highlights unresolved logarithmic behavior at critical regimes.
why: It would clarify the robustness of shape-constrained estimation when the true density is not log-concave.
key_works: Barber and Samworth, 2021, “Local continuity of log-concave projection, with applications to estimation under model misspecification,” arXiv:2002.06117, DOI:10.3150/20-BEJ1316.

title: Simultaneous calibration of generalized posteriors
open: Determine when one loss scale or learning-rate rule can provide calibrated uncertainty for several scientifically important functionals simultaneously under model misspecification.
status: General Bayesian updating is well established. A scalar adjustment can calibrate one target without necessarily correcting all directions or functionals.
why: It would prevent apparently coherent posterior summaries from having incompatible uncertainty interpretations.
key_works: Bissiri, Holmes, and Walker, 2016, “A General Framework for Updating Belief Distributions,” arXiv:1306.6430.

title: Computable prior-robust posterior envelopes
open: Construct certified upper and lower posterior expectations over explicitly defined neighborhoods of a prior, with algorithms that remain useful in high-dimensional hierarchical models.
status: Research target within Bayesian sensitivity analysis. The required deliverable is a tight, computationally certified envelope, not a small collection of alternative-prior fits.
why: It would quantify how much conclusions depend on poorly known prior choices.
key_works: Gelman et al., 2020, “Bayesian Workflow,” arXiv:2011.01808; Bissiri, Holmes, and Walker, 2016, “A General Framework for Updating Belief Distributions.”

title: Singular learning theory with growing architecture
open: Derive uniform learning-curve and marginal-likelihood expansions when a singular model’s architecture grows with sample size and its singularity type can change.
status: Fixed-model singular learning theory supplies a foundational framework. Growing mixtures, latent networks, and changing parameter dimensions require additional asymptotic theory.
why: It would improve model comparison for overparameterized latent-variable systems.
key_works: Watanabe, 2009, *Algebraic Geometry and Statistical Learning Theory*, DOI:10.1017/CBO9780511800474.

title: Principled selection of Bayesian feedback cuts
open: Choose which information flows to block in a modular Bayesian model using an explicit decision criterion, while accounting for uncertainty about which modules are misspecified.
status: Cut distributions and calibrated posterior-bootstrap alternatives already exist. Selecting cuts adaptively without invalidating the resulting uncertainty is a further problem.
why: It would replace ad hoc protection of trusted model components with an auditable rule.
key_works: Pompe, Kasprzak, and Jacob, 2026 revision, “Asymptotics of cut distributions and robust modular inference using Posterior Bootstrap,” arXiv:2110.11149v4.

title: Certified attribution of posterior sensitivity
open: Separate the contributions of prior choice, likelihood misspecification, numerical approximation, and data preprocessing to a posterior decision, with bounds that remain valid when these factors interact.
status: Proposed methodological target. Bayesian workflow provides diagnostic practices, but the requested result is a quantitative decomposition with certified remainder terms.
why: It would show which uncertainty source actually threatens a conclusion.
key_works: Gelman et al., 2020, “Bayesian Workflow,” arXiv:2011.01808; Blei, Kucukelbir, and McAuliffe, 2017, “Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians,” arXiv:1601.00670.

title: Generalized Bayes under adaptive, informative data collection
open: Develop generalized posterior updates whose uncertainty and decision guarantees remain interpretable when actions affect which observations arrive and the loss is itself adaptively chosen.
status: Research target extending loss-based updating beyond a fixed observational setup. Sequential validity cannot be assumed merely because updates are Bayesian in form.
why: It would support defensible inference in autonomous laboratories and adaptive decision systems.
key_works: Bissiri, Holmes, and Walker, 2016, “A General Framework for Updating Belief Distributions,” arXiv:1306.6430; Howard et al., 2021, “Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences,” arXiv:1810.08240.

title: Adaptive Bernstein–von Mises theory with unknown operators
open: Establish conditions for adaptive Bayesian uncertainty about nonlinear functionals when both the latent function and the inverse-problem operator are estimated from data.
status: Adaptive results exist in Gaussian white noise and other structured settings. Joint operator uncertainty and nonlinear functionals introduce further bias and identifiability issues.
why: It would connect flexible Bayesian reconstruction to honest scientific error bars.
key_works: Ray, 2014/2017, “Adaptive Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise,” arXiv:1407.3397; Castillo and Nickl, 2014, “On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures.”

title: High-dimensional empirical-Bayes regret with heterogeneous noise
open: Determine sharp oracle-regret rates for empirical-Bayes posterior means when observation dimension grows, noise covariance differs across units, and the mixing distribution is unknown.
status: Research target beyond scalar normal-means benchmarks. Existing multivariate and heteroskedastic methods do not automatically settle all growing-dimensional regimes.
why: It would quantify the benefit of borrowing strength in complex repeated estimation tasks.
key_works: Maleki et al., 2026, “High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems,” arXiv:2605.05076; Robbins, 1956, “An Empirical Bayes Approach to Statistics.”

title: Empirical Bayes with unknown cross-unit dependence
open: Construct empirical-Bayes estimators with sharp regret and valid uncertainty when nominally parallel estimation problems share an unknown, structured dependence matrix.
status: Independence enables many classical compound-decision arguments. The target requires learning dependence without counting shared information multiple times.
why: It would improve shrinkage for spatial, genetic, and repeated-experiment estimates.
key_works: Robbins, 1956, “An Empirical Bayes Approach to Statistics”; Gelman et al., 2020, “Bayesian Workflow,” arXiv:2011.01808.

title: Honest credible sets after regularity selection
open: Characterize the weakest practically meaningful restrictions under which hierarchical or empirical-Bayes credible sets adapt to unknown regularity while maintaining uniform frequentist coverage.
status: Positive coverage results exist for sieve priors and restricted parameter classes. Unrestricted adaptive honesty is impossible; sharp boundaries among usable restrictions remain important.
why: It would distinguish trustworthy uncertainty adaptation from merely attractive posterior contraction.
key_works: Rousseau and Szabó, 2020, “Asymptotic frequentist coverage properties of Bayesian credible sets for sieve priors,” DOI:10.1214/19-AOS1881; Ray, “Adaptive Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise,” arXiv:1407.3397.

title: Scientifically meaningful cluster counts under misspecification
open: Define and consistently infer a stable, scientifically interpretable cluster-count estimand when the data distribution is not exactly a finite mixture from the fitted component family.
status: Inconsistency of component-count inference for common process mixtures is established. The unresolved target is a robust estimand and corresponding uncertainty, not disproving that known result.
why: It would prevent arbitrary mixture components from being mistaken for real biological or social populations.
key_works: Miller and Harrison, 2014, “Inconsistency of Pitman-Yor process mixtures for the number of components,” arXiv:1309.0024; Watanabe, 2009, *Algebraic Geometry and Statistical Learning Theory*.

title: Empirical priors learned after selection
open: Derive valid posterior decision and coverage guarantees when the data used to estimate a prior have first been selected by significance, publication, or an adaptive screening procedure.
status: Proposed research target joining empirical Bayes and selective inference. Treating the selected sample as representative generally changes the prior-learning problem.
why: It would improve reuse of published effects and screened molecular measurements.
key_works: Lee et al., 2016, “Exact post-selection inference, with application to the lasso,” arXiv:1311.6238; Andrews and Kasy, 2019, “Identification of and Correction for Publication Bias,” DOI:10.1257/aer.20180310.

title: Certificates of unexplored posterior mass
subfield: Markov-chain Monte Carlo and posterior computation
open: Under explicit geometric assumptions on separated modes, construct computable upper bounds on posterior mass that a finite collection of chains may have missed.
status: Standard convergence diagnostics cannot certify arbitrary undiscovered modes. The open target is useful certification under stated restrictions, not an impossible universal diagnostic.
why: It would prevent seemingly converged chains from supporting confidently wrong decisions.
key_works: Vehtari et al., 2021, “Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC,” arXiv:1903.08008.

title: Complexity theory for practical NUTS
subfield: Markov-chain Monte Carlo and posterior computation
open: Prove end-to-end sampling complexity for realistically adapted No-U-Turn samplers, including step-size adaptation, mass-matrix learning, trajectory termination, and constrained parameter transformations.
status: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo has a substantial theoretical foundation; practical adaptive implementations combine mechanisms whose full guarantees require additional assumptions and analysis.
why: It would explain when a standard Bayesian workhorse can be trusted to scale.
key_works: Betancourt, 2017, “A Conceptual Introduction to Hamiltonian Monte Carlo,” arXiv:1701.02434.

title: Adaptive tempering through unknown phase transitions
subfield: Markov-chain Monte Carlo and posterior computation
open: Design temperature ladders and exchange schedules that adapt to unknown multimodal barriers while retaining quantitative mixing guarantees.
status: Proposed research target. Fixed schedules and model-specific analyses do not provide a universally effective adaptive method for phase-transition bottlenecks.
why: It would make multimodal posterior exploration less dependent on expert tuning.
key_works: Betancourt, 2017, “A Conceptual Introduction to Hamiltonian Monte Carlo,” arXiv:1701.02434; Vehtari et al., 2021, “Rank-normalization, folding, and localization.”

title: Dimension-scalable unbiased coupling
subfield: Markov-chain Monte Carlo and posterior computation
open: Construct coupled Markov chains with finite-variance unbiased estimators and meeting times that remain controlled as dimension, multimodality, and data size increase.
status: Unbiased MCMC through coupling is established. The open frontier concerns practical meeting-time and variance guarantees in difficult high-dimensional models.
why: It would permit parallel Monte Carlo with interpretable error accounting and less burn-in ambiguity.
key_works: Jacob, O’Leary, and Atchadé, 2020, “Unbiased Markov chain Monte Carlo with couplings,” arXiv:1708.03625.

title: Exact subsampling for broad nonconjugate models
subfield: Markov-chain Monte Carlo and posterior computation
open: Identify model classes permitting exact posterior sampling with genuinely sublinear average data access per effective draw, including the cost of preprocessing and control variates.
status: Proposed frontier question. Approximate minibatch methods, exact special cases, and expensive preprocessing must be separated when comparing complexity.
why: It would clarify whether exact Bayesian inference can avoid repeatedly scanning massive datasets.
key_works: Blei, Kucukelbir, and McAuliffe, 2017, “Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians,” arXiv:1601.00670; Jacob et al., 2020, “Unbiased Markov chain Monte Carlo with couplings.”

title: Tenfold lower energy per validated posterior estimate
subfield: Markov-chain Monte Carlo and posterior computation
open: Reduce measured energy by at least 10× on a preregistered suite while matching reference posterior-functional error, interval calibration, and failure rates; include compilation and warmup costs.
status: Proposed moonshot, not a claimed unmet universal hardware record. A baseline suite and measurement protocol must be frozen before comparison.
why: It would make large-scale uncertainty quantification materially cheaper and more accessible.
key_works: Gelman et al., 2020, “Bayesian Workflow,” arXiv:2011.01808; Vehtari et al., 2021, “Rank-normalization, folding, and localization.”

title: Computable functional-bias bounds for variational inference
open: Produce useful, computable bounds on errors in selected posterior expectations and tail probabilities from a fitted variational approximation, without requiring the exact posterior normalizing constant.
status: Variational objectives are tractable surrogates, but objective quality alone does not guarantee every scientific functional is accurate.
why: It would convert fast approximations into auditable inferential tools.
key_works: Blei, Kucukelbir, and McAuliffe, 2017, “Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians,” arXiv:1601.00670, DOI:10.1080/01621459.2017.1285773.

title: Variational mode-weight certification
open: Certify relative masses of separated posterior modes using variational approximations, including a bound on omitted modes under explicit model restrictions.
status: Research target distinct from fitting multimodal variational families. Representing several modes does not certify their weights or completeness.
why: It would improve Bayesian model ambiguity and rare-hypothesis assessment.
key_works: Blei, Kucukelbir, and McAuliffe, 2017, “Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians,” arXiv:1601.00670.

title: Out-of-distribution calibration of amortized posteriors
open: Detect and quantify posterior miscalibration when observations lie outside the simulator or training distribution, while distinguishing extrapolation from genuine model incompatibility.
status: Simulation-based inference benchmarks establish useful in-distribution comparisons. The proposed target requires coverage and abstention guarantees under specified shifts.
why: It would reduce dangerous confidence in simulator-trained scientific inference.
key_works: Cranmer, Brehmer, and Louppe, 2020, “The frontier of simulation-based inference,” arXiv:1911.01429; Lueckmann et al., 2021, “Benchmarking Simulation-Based Inference,” PMLR 130.

title: Separating simulator discrepancy from physical parameters
open: Characterize which experimental designs identify physical parameters separately from flexible simulator discrepancy, and obtain uncertainty that acknowledges remaining nonidentifiability.
status: Calibration can trade parameter changes against discrepancy terms. The target is design-specific identifiability and sharp uncertainty, not simply adding a discrepancy process.
why: It would prevent calibrated simulators from returning physically misleading parameter estimates.
key_works: Cranmer, Brehmer, and Louppe, 2020, “The frontier of simulation-based inference,” arXiv:1911.01429; Gelman et al., 2020, “Bayesian Workflow.”

title: Calibration tests targeted to rare posterior failures
open: Build simulation-based validation procedures with quantified power against localized failures affecting rare parameter regions, tails, or scientifically selected subgroups.
status: Proposed testing target. Aggregate benchmark scores can conceal low-frequency failures; the required contribution is a power analysis and controlled multiplicity.
why: It would detect errors that matter scientifically despite looking small on average.
key_works: Lueckmann et al., 2021, “Benchmarking Simulation-Based Inference,” PMLR 130; Morris, White, and Crowther, 2019, “Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods,” DOI:10.1002/sim.8086.

title: Reliable likelihood ratios for rare simulator events
open: Estimate likelihood ratios accurately enough for rare-event tests and posterior odds when relevant observations occur far less frequently than ordinary simulator training examples.
status: Research target within simulation-based inference. Average predictive accuracy does not supply uniform tail-ratio guarantees.
why: It would strengthen anomaly searches and rare-phenomenon inference.
key_works: Cranmer, Brehmer, and Louppe, 2020, “The frontier of simulation-based inference,” arXiv:1911.01429; Engelke and Ivanovs, 2021, “Sparse Structures for Multivariate Extremes,” arXiv:2004.12182.

title: Complete admissibility theory for e-processes
open: Give necessary and sufficient conditions for admissibility of e-processes under broad composite nulls, including when one process uniformly improves another.
status: Martingale-based necessity results are established; the 2023 safe-inference survey lists broader admissibility questions.
why: It would distinguish fundamentally efficient sequential evidence from avoidable conservatism.
key_works: Ramdas, Ruf, Larsson, and Koolen, 2020, “Admissible anytime-valid sequential inference must rely on nonnegative martingales,” arXiv:2009.03167.

title: Existence of nontrivial e-processes for composite nulls
open: Characterize exactly which composite hypotheses admit nontrivial, powerful e-processes relative to a specified filtration and alternative class.
status: Convex-geometric and martingale approaches provide partial answers. The general existence and usefulness boundary remains an explicit research direction.
why: It would identify when safe optional stopping can provide real evidence rather than only trivial guarantees.
key_works: Ramdas, Grünwald, Vovk, and Shafer, 2023, “Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference,” arXiv:2210.01948, DOI:10.1214/23-STS894.

title: Optimal filtration reduction
open: Determine how much data history should be retained in the filtration to permit powerful valid e-processes while avoiding unnecessary nuisance restrictions.
status: Filtration choice is an explicit issue in safe sequential inference. Coarsening can enable validity but discard information; the sharp tradeoff is not generally characterized.
why: It would guide the design of evidence processes for dependent and nuisance-rich data.
key_works: Ramdas et al., 2023, “Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference,” arXiv:2210.01948.

title: Time-consistent reverse information projections
open: Identify conditions under which one-step reverse-information projections combine into a time-consistent, globally efficient sequential testing strategy.
status: Information-projection constructions are powerful in fixed experiments; extending their optimality coherently through time is an explicit open direction.
why: It would connect local betting choices to globally efficient evidence accumulation.
key_works: Ramdas et al., 2023, “Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference,” arXiv:2210.01948.

title: Sharp power theory for universal inference
open: Characterize the best achievable power and confidence-set size for universal-inference constructions, including optimal splitting, aggregation, and nuisance fitting.
status: Finite-sample validity is established for broad likelihood-based settings. Sharp efficiency relative to model-specific procedures remains the stronger target.
why: It would show when broad applicability costs little and when it is prohibitively conservative.
key_works: Wasserman, Ramdas, and Balakrishnan, 2020, “Universal Inference,” arXiv:1912.11436.

title: Moment-adaptive confidence sequences under dependence
open: Construct confidence sequences adapting to unknown tail and dependence parameters within explicit bounded-moment and mixing envelopes, with matching lower bounds.
status: Time-uniform nonparametric confidence sequences are well developed. Unrestricted finite-variance adaptation must not be confused with the restricted, attainable problem posed here.
why: It would enable continuous monitoring of heavy-tailed operational data.
key_works: Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe, and Sekhon, 2021, “Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences,” arXiv:1810.08240.

title: Model-X inference with learned covariate distributions
open: Obtain sharp false-discovery guarantees when the covariate distribution used to construct knockoffs is learned imperfectly, with uncertainty that adapts to where misspecification matters.
status: Model-X knockoffs provide guarantees under appropriate distributional knowledge. Robustness to estimated conditional laws is an active extension, not an automatic consequence.
why: It would make conditional variable discovery less dependent on an unverifiable generative model.
key_works: Candès, Fan, Janson, and Lv, 2018, “Panning for Gold: Model-X Knockoffs for High-dimensional Controlled Variable Selection,” arXiv:1610.02351.

title: Knockoff power under near-collinearity
open: Characterize the maximal attainable power of valid knockoff procedures when predictors form nearly indistinguishable groups, and determine optimal transitions between individual and group discoveries.
status: False-discovery control and group-oriented methods exist. The unresolved target is a sharp power and identifiability frontier under extreme correlation.
why: It would prevent low power from being mistaken for absence of relevant predictors.
key_works: Barber and Candès, 2015, “Controlling the false discovery rate via knockoffs,” arXiv:1404.5609; Candès et al., 2018, “Panning for Gold.”

title: Online FDR with dependent, delayed outcomes
open: Develop online false-discovery procedures that exploit specified dependence while handling outcome delays correlated with effect size and ongoing adaptive experiment selection.
status: Online FDR methods and positive-dependence extensions exist. Jointly informative delays and adaptive test generation require additional analysis.
why: It would support continuously running experimentation platforms.
key_works: Ramdas, Zrnic, Wainwright, and Jordan, 2018, “SAFFRON: an adaptive algorithm for online control of the false discovery rate,” arXiv:1802.09098; Fisher, “Online false discovery rate control for LORD++ and SAFFRON under positive dependence,” DOI:10.1002/bimj.202300177.

title: Optimal e-value testing under structured dependence
open: Determine minimax discovery power for e-value procedures over specified block-dependence classes, and quantify when dependence information improves on arbitrary-dependence-safe rules.
status: e-BH provides broad FDR control. The target is sharp power under additional externally justified structure, not basic validity under dependence.
why: It would reduce unnecessary conservatism in correlated testing problems.
key_works: Wang and Ramdas, 2022, “False discovery rate control with e-values,” arXiv:2009.02824.

title: Error control for adaptively constructed hypothesis hierarchies
open: Control false discoveries simultaneously across levels when the hierarchy of groups and subgroups is learned from the same data used for testing.
status: Research target combining structured testing and adaptive analysis. A fixed hierarchy is materially simpler than one chosen to make discoveries look coherent.
why: It would support reliable pathway, ontology, and subgroup discovery.
key_works: Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis,” arXiv:1411.2664; Wang and Ramdas, 2022, “False discovery rate control with e-values.”

title: Simultaneous signs and magnitudes after discovery selection
open: Construct useful confidence statements for effect signs and magnitudes after adaptive FDR-based selection, including data-driven changes to the reported family.
status: Selective inference and multiple-testing theory provide separate tools. The target is a coherent joint guarantee with near-optimal interval lengths.
why: It would improve interpretation of discoveries beyond a binary significance label.
key_works: Lee et al., 2016, “Exact post-selection inference, with application to the lasso,” arXiv:1311.6238; Barber and Candès, 2015, “Controlling the false discovery rate via knockoffs.”

title: Selective inference after deep clustering
subfield: Selective inference and adaptive data analysis
open: Derive valid uncertainty for differences between clusters produced by a learned nonlinear representation, including selection of architecture, cluster count, and comparison.
status: Exact selective methods exist for tractable selection events. Deep clustering generally produces a much more complicated data-dependent event.
why: It would prevent algorithmically manufactured groups from generating spurious scientific findings.
key_works: Lee et al., 2016, “Exact post-selection inference, with application to the lasso,” arXiv:1311.6238; Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis.”

title: Black-box selective inference for complete pipelines
subfield: Selective inference and adaptive data analysis
open: Obtain computationally feasible selective inference for pipelines whose selection behavior is available only through execution, while quantifying approximation error in the inferred selection law.
status: Proposed research target. Re-running a black box is not itself a guarantee that its selection bias has been measured or corrected.
why: It would extend principled inference to real software pipelines rather than only analytically simple selectors.
key_works: Lee et al., 2016, “Exact post-selection inference, with application to the lasso,” arXiv:1311.6238; Morris et al., 2019, “Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods,” DOI:10.1002/sim.8086.

title: Inference over analyst-selected multiverses
subfield: Selective inference and adaptive data analysis
open: Quantify uncertainty when analysts explore many defensible specifications and choose which subset to report, without assuming the explored set was fixed in advance.
status: Many-analyst studies demonstrate substantial analytic variability. The target is valid inference for adaptive exploration, not merely displaying a specification curve.
why: It would make robustness analysis resistant to its own selection bias.
key_works: Botvinik-Nezer et al., 2020, “Variability in the analysis of a single neuroimaging dataset by many teams,” DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-2314-9; Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis.”

title: Reusable holdouts for structured scientific queries
subfield: Selective inference and adaptive data analysis
open: Determine optimal accuracy–reuse tradeoffs when adaptive queries share scientific structure, such as nested models, common outcomes, or a limited causal graph.
status: General adaptive-data-analysis guarantees establish useful baselines. Exploiting structure without silently losing protection remains a sharper frontier.
why: It would let scarce validation data support more legitimate scientific questions.
key_works: Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis,” arXiv:1411.2664.

title: Cross-validation uncertainty under weak algorithmic stability
subfield: Selective inference and adaptive data analysis
open: Construct informative confidence intervals for prediction risk after cross-validation-based model selection under explicitly weak stability and dependence assumptions.
status: There is no universally unbiased estimator of K-fold cross-validation variance. That negative result does not settle restricted, calibrated intervals for modern unstable learners.
why: It would make reported differences between predictive models more trustworthy.
key_works: Bengio and Grandvalet, 2004, “No Unbiased Estimator of the Variance of K-Fold Cross-Validation,” JMLR 5:1089–1105.

title: Winner’s-curse correction for adaptive leaderboards
subfield: Selective inference and adaptive data analysis
open: Estimate the true performance of an adaptively selected leaderboard winner while accounting for repeated submissions, shared training lineages, and hidden test-set feedback.
status: Proposed benchmark-inference target. Fixed-family multiplicity correction does not capture an evolving ecosystem of correlated submissions.
why: It would make benchmark leadership a more meaningful scientific claim.
key_works: Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis,” arXiv:1411.2664; Bengio and Grandvalet, 2004, “No Unbiased Estimator of the Variance of K-Fold Cross-Validation.”

title: Conditional coverage versus prediction-set size
open: Determine sharp achievable tradeoffs among approximate conditional coverage, the complexity of the conditioning family, and expected prediction-set volume.
status: Exact unrestricted distribution-free conditional coverage is already ruled out in useful settings. The open problem concerns nontrivial restricted or approximate guarantees.
why: It would clarify what “reliable for people like this” can actually mean.
key_works: Barber, Candès, Ramdas, and Tibshirani, 2019/2021, “The limits of distribution-free conditional predictive inference,” arXiv:1903.04684.

title: Conformal prediction with uncertain shift weights
open: Construct sharp finite-sample coverage bounds when covariate-shift importance weights are estimated, potentially misspecified, and unstable in low-overlap regions.
status: Weighted and doubly robust calibration methods exist. The target is a complete finite-sample uncertainty accounting for the weights themselves.
why: It would improve prediction after deployment populations change.
key_works: Yang, Kuchibhotla, and Tchetgen Tchetgen, 2024, “Doubly robust calibration of prediction sets under covariate shift,” JRSS B 86:943–965; Barber et al., 2023, “Conformal prediction beyond exchangeability,” arXiv:2202.13415.

title: Coverage with drift and selectively delayed labels
open: Maintain useful predictive coverage when outcomes arrive late, delay depends on the outcome, and the data distribution changes before feedback becomes available.
status: Adaptive conformal methods handle important time-series settings. Informative delays add a missing-data problem to the adaptation problem.
why: It would support calibrated predictions in medicine, lending, and long-horizon operations.
key_works: Zaffran et al., 2022, “Adaptive conformal predictions for time series,” ICML, pp. 25834–25866; Barber et al., “Conformal prediction beyond exchangeability,” arXiv:2202.13415.

title: Censored prediction with explicit identification horizons
open: Produce prediction sets for event times that separate uncertainty within identifiable follow-up horizons from irreducible ambiguity beyond them, allowing estimated censoring mechanisms.
status: Research target extending conformal and survival methods. A nominal coverage statement should not conceal assumptions about unobserved long-term outcomes.
why: It would improve interpretation of survival-time predictions under limited follow-up.
key_works: Angelopoulos and Bates, 2021/2023, “A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification,” arXiv:2107.07511; STRATOS Topic Group 8, “Survival Analysis.”

title: Efficient structured prediction sets
open: Construct statistically efficient prediction sets for graphs, trajectories, or combinatorial objects that are also compactly representable and computationally searchable.
status: Structured conformal methods exist, including trajectory forecasting. Coverage alone does not settle representation size, usefulness, or optimality of set geometry.
why: It would make predictive uncertainty actionable for planning and scientific interpretation.
key_works: Zhou, Lindemann, and Sesia, 2024, “Conformalized adaptive forecasting of heterogeneous trajectories,” PMLR 235:62002–62056; Angelopoulos and Bates, “A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction.”

title: Reusing calibration data after model selection
open: Characterize optimal prediction-set efficiency when calibration observations influence model selection, aggregation, and final interval construction.
status: Selection and aggregation methods are available. The open target is the sharp price of arbitrary but controlled reuse, rather than declaring all reuse invalid.
why: It would reduce waste of scarce labeled data.
key_works: Yang and Kuchibhotla, 2025, “Selection and aggregation of conformal prediction sets,” JASA 120:435–447; Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis.”

title: Weak-proxy robust proximal inference
open: Construct confidence sets for causal effects that remain valid as proxy bridge equations become weakly identified or nearly nonunique.
status: Proximal identification and estimation frameworks are established. Weak bridges create an inverse-problem analogue of weak instruments.
why: It would prevent weak proxy measurements from producing misleadingly precise causal claims.
key_works: Tchetgen Tchetgen, Ying, Cui, Shi, and Miao, 2020, “An Introduction to Proximal Causal Learning,” arXiv:2009.10982; Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen, 2018, “Identifying causal effects with proxy variables of an unmeasured confounder.”

title: Finite-sample discovery of latent cyclic causal systems
open: Derive computationally feasible confidence statements for causal equivalence classes in nonlinear cyclic systems with latent confounding, under explicit stability and faithfulness margins.
status: Cyclic causal discovery and partial-ancestral-graph results exist. The target is finite-sample reliability and scalability, not the first treatment of feedback.
why: It would support causal analysis of systems that genuinely contain feedback loops.
key_works: Mooij and Claassen, 2020, “Constraint-Based Causal Discovery using Partial Ancestral Graphs in the presence of Cycles,” PMLR 124:1159–1168.

title: Transportability with unmeasured effect modifiers
open: Derive sharp transported-effect bounds when source and target populations differ through partially unmeasured effect modifiers, with sensitivity parameters tied to plausible external information.
status: Transportability and generalization frameworks provide identification under stated assumptions. Unmeasured population differences require partial identification rather than automatic transport.
why: It would clarify when trial results support decisions in a different population.
key_works: Bareinboim and Pearl, 2016, “Causal inference and the data-fusion problem,” PNAS 113:7345–7352; Tipton and Olsen, 2018, “A Review of Statistical Methods for Generalizing From Evaluations of Educational Interventions,” DOI:10.3102/0013189X18781522.

title: Minimal validation designs for causal measurement error
open: Determine which combinations of repeated measurements, validation subsamples, and randomized measurement devices identify causal effects when errors are nonlinear and correlated.
status: Proxy-variable identification supplies useful special cases. A design-level characterization for dependent errors is a more specific outstanding target.
why: It would tell investigators what extra measurements are actually worth collecting.
key_works: Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen, 2018, “Identifying causal effects with proxy variables of an unmeasured confounder”; Tchetgen Tchetgen et al., 2020, “An Introduction to Proximal Causal Learning,” arXiv:2009.10982.

title: Identification of longitudinal nonignorable missingness
open: Characterize which longitudinal causal queries become identifiable after adding specified shadow variables or recontact measurements, allowing latent common causes and treatment–missingness feedback.
status: General missing-data and proximal frameworks address important cases. A complete characterization for a clearly specified longitudinal graph class remains a research target.
why: It would guide data collection in studies where dropout is related to unobserved health or behavior.
key_works: Tchetgen Tchetgen et al., 2020, “An Introduction to Proximal Causal Learning,” arXiv:2009.10982; Cinelli et al., 2025, “Challenges in Statistics: A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference,” arXiv:2508.17099.

title: Causal synthesis across incompatible datasets
open: Combine datasets with different measured variables, populations, and interventions while jointly learning uncertain causal structure and estimating target-population effects.
status: Causal data fusion is established when sufficient graph and population-shift information is known. Joint discovery, covariate mismatch, and effect estimation are explicitly identified as open challenges.
why: It would turn fragmented studies into defensible cumulative causal knowledge.
key_works: Bareinboim and Pearl, 2016, “Causal inference and the data-fusion problem”; Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen, 2020, “Joint causal inference from multiple contexts,” JMLR 21(99).

title: Heterogeneous-effect inference under weak overlap
open: Derive minimax confidence bands for conditional treatment effects when overlap deteriorates with sample size and effect smoothness is unknown.
status: Flexible treatment-effect estimation is mature in important regimes. Uniform uncertainty, bias adaptation, and weak overlap interact in ways not settled by prediction rates alone.
why: It would identify which personalized treatment recommendations are supported by data.
key_works: Cinelli et al., 2025, “Challenges in Statistics: A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference,” arXiv:2508.17099; Bull, 2012, “Honest adaptive confidence bands and self-similar functions.”

title: Policy-value inference after learning under interference
open: Obtain valid confidence bounds for the value of a learned treatment-allocation policy when one person’s treatment affects others and the policy is selected using the same network data.
status: Policy learning and randomization-based interference inference have substantial separate literatures. Their joint post-selection problem is more demanding.
why: It would support defensible rollout of network-wide interventions.
key_works: Aronow and Samii, 2017, “Estimating Average Causal Effects Under General Interference, with Application to a Social Network Experiment,” arXiv:1305.6156; Athey and Wager, 2021, “Policy Learning With Observational Data.”

title: Learning the exposure mapping
open: Identify or partially identify causal effects when the mapping from neighbors’ treatment assignments to an individual’s effective exposure is unknown and must be learned.
status: General-interference frameworks often specify an exposure mapping. Estimating that mapping without invalidating inference is a distinct unresolved component.
why: It would reduce dependence on arbitrary definitions of spillover exposure.
key_works: Aronow and Samii, 2017, “Estimating Average Causal Effects Under General Interference,” arXiv:1305.6156.

title: Sensitivity analysis for a misspecified interference network
open: Derive sharp effect bounds when the observed network omits or invents edges, with error constraints informed by a network-validation sample.
status: Proposed research target extending known-network interference inference. Network measurement error changes both exposure assignment and dependence.
why: It would make spillover estimates robust to imperfect social and contact networks.
key_works: Aronow and Samii, 2017, “Estimating Average Causal Effects Under General Interference,” arXiv:1305.6156; Binette and Steorts, 2022, “(Almost) All of Entity Resolution,” arXiv:2008.04443.

title: Sharp bounds for interacting multiple mediators
open: Obtain computable sharp bounds for mechanism-specific effects when multiple mediators interact, their ordering is partly unknown, and mediator–outcome confounding cannot be excluded.
status: Mediation estimands and identification strategies are established. The target combines uncertain ordering, interactions, and explicit partial identification.
why: It would help distinguish plausible mechanisms without pretending all pathway assumptions are known.
key_works: VanderWeele, 2015, *Explanation in Causal Inference: Methods for Mediation and Interaction*; Cinelli et al., 2025, “A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference,” arXiv:2508.17099.

title: Causal contagion with an evolving unobserved network
open: Separate contagion, homophily, and network evolution when ties are incompletely observed and both behavior and interventions alter future ties.
status: Proposed identification and inference target. Assuming a fixed observed network bypasses the central feedback and latent-selection difficulties.
why: It would improve causal claims about behavioral spread and epidemic interventions.
key_works: Cinelli et al., 2025, “A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference,” arXiv:2508.17099; Mooij and Claassen, 2020, “Constraint-Based Causal Discovery … in the presence of Cycles.”

title: Adaptive cluster trials with finite-sample guarantees
open: Design cluster-randomized trials that adapt allocation or recruitment while controlling finite-sample error under unequal cluster sizes and within-cluster interference.
status: Complex experiments are an explicit causal-inference challenge. The target combines adaptation, cluster imbalance, and dependence rather than treating each separately.
why: It would improve efficient experimentation in schools, hospitals, and communities.
key_works: Cinelli et al., 2025, “A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference,” arXiv:2508.17099; Howard et al., 2021, “Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences.”

title: Empirical validation of long-term surrogate outcomes
open: Build multi-intervention longitudinal datasets that test whether a surrogate predicts treatment effects on long-term outcomes across genuinely new interventions and populations.
status: Proposed experimental target. Surrogate-index methodology exists; predictive association within historical data is weaker than validated transport of causal treatment effects.
why: It would show when short experiments can responsibly replace years of follow-up.
key_works: Athey, Chetty, Imbens, and Kang, 2019, “The surrogate index: Combining short-term proxies to estimate long-term treatment effects more rapidly and precisely,” NBER Working Paper 26463.

title: Switchback experiments with unknown carryover
open: Jointly choose switching schedules and estimate treatment effects when carryover duration is unknown, potentially heterogeneous, and comparable to the experimental horizon.
status: Online experimentation has developed many specialized designs. Unknown carryover makes both randomization choice and uncertainty calibration harder.
why: It would improve experiments in marketplaces, logistics, and shared infrastructure.
key_works: Larsen et al., 2024, “Statistical challenges in online controlled experiments: A review of A/B testing methodology,” *The American Statistician* 78:135–149.

title: Multi-objective adaptive experimentation
open: Characterize the attainable tradeoff between statistical information, participant welfare, allocation fairness, and cumulative reward in adaptive experiments.
status: Proposed decision-theoretic target. Optimizing one scalar reward does not automatically solve uncertainty or fairness constraints.
why: It would make adaptive experiments useful without obscuring who bears their costs.
key_works: Cinelli et al., 2025, “A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference,” arXiv:2508.17099; Larsen et al., 2024, “Statistical challenges in online controlled experiments.”

title: Cost-optimal causal intervention discovery
open: Select interventions that identify a target causal query at minimum expected cost when interventions have heterogeneous expense, feasibility, and uncertain effects on observability.
status: Research target beyond intervention counting. A solution should provide approximation guarantees or hardness results for an explicit graph and cost class.
why: It would focus expensive experiments on the information that actually changes a decision.
key_works: Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen, 2020, “Joint causal inference from multiple contexts”; “Design of Experiment for Discovering Directed Mixed Graph,” 2025–2026, arXiv:2509.01887.

title: Adaptive factorial designs with sparse high-order interactions
open: Find designs that adaptively locate rare high-order interactions while controlling false discoveries and quantifying the cost of not assuming strong heredity.
status: Proposed target connecting factorial design and modern sparse testing. Restricting attention to main effects or inherited interactions changes the problem.
why: It would reveal combinations of interventions that simple A/B tests miss.
key_works: Larsen et al., 2024, “Statistical challenges in online controlled experiments”; Barber and Candès, 2015, “Controlling the false discovery rate via knockoffs,” arXiv:1404.5609.

title: High-dimensional adaptive confidence sets under nonignorable missingness
subfield: Missing data, measurement error, and record linkage
open: Develop joint confidence regions for multivariate parameters that adapt to the amount of nonignorable missingness under explicit contamination and moment classes.
status: A September 2026 paper establishes adaptive confidence intervals in particular missing-data mean problems. The multivariate joint-coverage extension posed here is not that already-resolved scalar problem.
why: It would support simultaneous conclusions from incomplete high-dimensional measurements.
key_works: Ma, Verchand, Gao, and Samworth, 2026, “Adaptive confidence intervals with missing data,” arXiv:2609.28336.

title: Randomized recontact designs for missingness validation
subfield: Missing data, measurement error, and record linkage
open: Design and execute randomized recontact studies that estimate how outcomes among initial nonresponders differ from responders, including the effect of contact intensity on measurement.
status: Proposed experimental target. Its success criterion is recoverable validation information with documented residual nonresponse—not assuming expensive follow-up eliminates selection.
why: It would turn untestable missingness assumptions into partially measurable quantities.
key_works: Wu, 2022, “Statistical inference with non-probability survey samples”; Ma et al., 2026, “Adaptive confidence intervals with missing data,” arXiv:2609.28336.

title: Downstream inference with uncertain entity linkage
subfield: Missing data, measurement error, and record linkage
open: Produce confidence intervals for regression and causal estimands that integrate uncertainty over possible record linkages, including dependence between linkage quality and the outcome.
status: Probabilistic linkage and entity resolution are mature topics. Treating one estimated linkage as truth can omit a material source of uncertainty.
why: It would improve the reliability of linked administrative and health records.
key_works: Binette and Steorts, 2022, “(Almost) All of Entity Resolution,” arXiv:2008.04443, DOI:10.1126/sciadv.abi8021.

title: Nonlinear measurement error with unknown error law
subfield: Missing data, measurement error, and record linkage
open: Identify and estimate nonlinear regression or causal functionals when measurement error is heteroskedastic, dependent across instruments, and learned from limited validation data.
status: Research target requiring an explicit identifiable model class. Unrestricted error and signal distributions cannot simply be separated from noisy observations.
why: It would improve inference from imperfect assays, sensors, and self-reported measurements.
key_works: Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen, 2018, “Identifying causal effects with proxy variables of an unmeasured confounder”; QIBA Technical Performance Working Group, 2015, “Quantitative Imaging Biomarkers: A Review of Statistical Methods for Technical Performance Assessment.”

title: Tail inference under informative truncation
subfield: Missing data, measurement error, and record linkage
open: Derive sharp bounds for tail probabilities and extreme quantiles when observations enter a dataset only above or below an unknown selection boundary.
status: Proposed partial-identification target. Tail extrapolation must explicitly distinguish information in observed data from assumptions about excluded observations.
why: It would improve risk estimation in selected registries and detection-limited datasets.
key_works: Engelke and Ivanovs, 2021, “Sparse Structures for Multivariate Extremes,” arXiv:2004.12182; Liu et al., 2024/2026, “Statistical Inference with Nonignorable Non-Probability Survey Samples,” arXiv:2410.02920.

title: Imputation valid for adaptively chosen analyses
subfield: Missing data, measurement error, and record linkage
open: Develop imputation procedures and uncertainty rules that remain valid for a declared class of downstream analyses selected after inspecting the imputed data.
status: Proposed target extending congeniality and adaptive-analysis concerns. Validity for one prespecified analysis does not establish validity for an unrestricted analytic search.
why: It would make reusable completed datasets less likely to produce undercovered conclusions.
key_works: Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis,” arXiv:1411.2664; Gelman et al., 2020, “Bayesian Workflow,” arXiv:2011.01808.

title: Sharp inference for nonprobability samples with uncertain selection
open: Construct sharp population-estimand bounds and confidence sets when participation depends on unobserved outcomes but auxiliary probability samples constrain the selection mechanism.
status: Nonprobability-sample inference is an established research area; recent work treats nonignorable selection. The target is sharp, interpretable sensitivity rather than unconditional representativeness.
why: It would improve use of opt-in panels and platform data.
key_works: Wu, 2022, “Statistical inference with non-probability survey samples”; Liu, Yuan, Li, and Wu, 2024/2026, “Statistical Inference with Nonignorable Non-Probability Survey Samples,” arXiv:2410.02920.

title: Small-area uncertainty for domains with no direct observations
open: Provide honest uncertainty for small-area estimates when some domains have zero sampled units and borrowing assumptions may fail locally.
status: Proposed target within small-area estimation. Purely model-based prediction is possible, but distinguishing sampling information from unvalidated cross-area borrowing is essential.
why: It would improve interpretation of highly granular public statistics.
key_works: Wu, 2022, “Statistical inference with non-probability survey samples”; World Bank, “Statistical Performance Indicators” framework.

title: Capture–recapture with unseen heterogeneity
open: Characterize population-size bounds under heterogeneous capture probabilities and dependent lists, using limited linkage validation and substantively defensible restrictions.
status: Proposed synthesis target. Unseen individuals and dependence make unrestricted point identification unattainable; useful bounds require explicit additional information.
why: It would improve estimates of hidden populations and undercounted events.
key_works: Orlitsky, Suresh, and Wu, 2016, “Optimal prediction of the number of unseen species”; Binette and Steorts, 2022, “(Almost) All of Entity Resolution.”

title: Inclusion probabilities in adaptive multimode surveys
open: Recover valid design-based or explicitly model-assisted inference when recruitment channels, contact intensities, and sampling frames adapt during fieldwork.
status: Research target extending survey weighting to evolving designs. Logging the design is necessary but does not alone recover unknown selection probabilities.
why: It would allow operationally efficient surveys without silently abandoning representativeness.
key_works: Wu, 2022, “Statistical inference with non-probability survey samples”; Meng, 2022, “Miniaturizing data defect correlation: A versatile strategy for handling non-probability samples.”

title: Uncertainty for statistical revisions and vintages
open: Build joint predictive distributions for initial releases, later revisions, and final estimands that account for changing data sources and revision policies.
status: Proposed official-statistics target. Reporting sampling error for a final series does not describe uncertainty faced by users of early vintages.
why: It would improve decisions made from preliminary economic and demographic indicators.
key_works: World Bank, “Statistical Performance Indicators” framework; Truong, Oudre, and Vayatis, 2020, “Selective review of offline change point detection methods,” arXiv:1801.00718.

title: Private fine-geography estimates with full error accounting
open: Construct useful small-geography estimates whose intervals account jointly for survey design, nonresponse adjustment, disclosure noise, and postprocessing.
status: Proposed integration target. Privacy mechanisms and survey estimators each have theory, but their combined released-product uncertainty needs explicit validation.
why: It would make privacy-protected public statistics easier to interpret responsibly.
key_works: Duchi, Jordan, and Wainwright, 2018, “Minimax optimal procedures for locally private estimation,” DOI:10.1080/01621459.2017.1389735; Wu, 2022, “Statistical inference with non-probability survey samples.”

title: Efficient sample-optimal pure-private sparse means
open: Achieve information-theoretically optimal sample complexity for pure differentially private sparse Gaussian mean estimation with a polynomial-time algorithm, or establish a matching computational barrier.
status: Explicitly highlighted in the 2025 robust-statistics open-problem lecture; privacy-induced computational gaps are established in related sparse estimation settings.
why: It would make strong privacy practical for high-dimensional population estimation.
key_works: Georgiev and Hopkins, 2022, “Privacy Induces Robustness: Information-Computation Gaps and Sparse Mean Estimation,” arXiv:2211.00724; UW CSE 599K, 2025, “Lecture 18.”

title: Tail-adaptive local privacy
open: Determine which tail classes permit locally private estimators and confidence sets to adapt to unknown scale and moment bounds without sacrificing minimax rates.
status: Local-private minimax theory provides a foundation. Unknown tails complicate clipping, sensitivity, and adaptation simultaneously.
why: It would reduce reliance on arbitrary fixed clipping thresholds.
key_works: Duchi, Jordan, and Wainwright, 2018, “Minimax optimal procedures for locally private estimation,” DOI:10.1080/01621459.2017.1389735.

title: User-level private inference with unequal contribution sizes
open: Derive sharp confidence intervals when users contribute highly unequal numbers of correlated records, under user-level rather than record-level privacy.
status: Proposed target. Treating every record as independent both overstates effective sample size and misstates the privacy unit.
why: It would improve privacy-preserving analysis of longitudinal and platform data.
key_works: Duchi, Jordan, and Wainwright, 2018, “Minimax optimal procedures for locally private estimation”; Kairouz et al., 2021, “Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning,” arXiv:1912.04977.

title: Private causal inference for rare subgroups
open: Characterize the privacy–overlap–precision frontier for causal effects in rare subgroups, including honest decisions to report only bounds or abstain.
status: Proposed research target. Small subgroup size and extreme weighting can make privacy noise and identification weakness compound.
why: It would clarify when privacy-preserving equity analysis is statistically informative.
key_works: Duchi, Jordan, and Wainwright, 2018, “Minimax optimal procedures for locally private estimation”; Cinelli et al., 2025, “A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference.”

title: Synthetic data with valid adaptive downstream uncertainty
open: Release private synthetic data supporting a declared, adaptively queried class of estimands with confidence guarantees that include synthesis and privacy error.
status: Proposed target stronger than matching selected marginals or predicting held-out records. Universal fidelity to unrestricted downstream analyses is not assumed possible.
why: It would make synthetic releases useful for inference rather than only exploration.
key_works: Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis,” arXiv:1411.2664; Duchi, Jordan, and Wainwright, 2018, “Minimax optimal procedures for locally private estimation.”

title: Continual private change detection
open: Obtain matching detection-delay lower and upper bounds for continual private monitoring under unknown change times, dependent observations, and a limited lifetime privacy budget.
status: Proposed frontier combining change detection and privacy accounting. Repeatedly applying a one-time private test does not establish optimal lifetime performance.
why: It would enable privacy-preserving public-health and operational alerts.
key_works: Truong, Oudre, and Vayatis, 2020, “Selective review of offline change point detection methods,” arXiv:1801.00718; Howard et al., 2021, “Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences.”

title: Communication-optimal nonparametric confidence sets
open: Determine the minimum communication needed for honest, adaptive nonparametric confidence sets when clients have heterogeneous distributions and unequal sample sizes.
status: Distributed estimation lower bounds exist. Confidence-set adaptation and heterogeneity create additional requirements beyond point-estimation accuracy.
why: It would identify which uncertainty guarantees can survive severe communication limits.
key_works: Duchi, Jordan, Wainwright, and Zhang, 2014, “Optimality guarantees for distributed statistical estimation,” arXiv:1405.0782.

title: Inference under informative client participation
open: Identify population targets and construct valid intervals when clients’ availability and participation depend on unobserved outcomes or local model errors.
status: Client heterogeneity and participation are recognized federated-learning challenges. Random-participation analyses do not settle informative participation.
why: It would prevent available devices or institutions from being mistaken for the target population.
