key_works: Kairouz et al., 2021, “Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning,” arXiv:1912.04977; Wu, 2022, “Statistical inference with non-probability survey samples.”

title: Borrowing strength without negative-transfer overconfidence
open: Construct federated estimators that adaptively borrow information across sites while giving valid uncertainty when some sites are incompatible with the target site.
status: Personalization and heterogeneous learning methods exist. A no-harm guarantee for uncertainty is stronger than an average prediction improvement.
why: It would make cross-institution collaboration safer for unusual or underserved populations.
key_works: Kairouz et al., 2021, “Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning,” arXiv:1912.04977; Pompe, Kasprzak, and Jacob, 2026, “Asymptotics of cut distributions and robust modular inference using Posterior Bootstrap.”

title: Byzantine robustness compatible with secure aggregation
open: Design protocols that simultaneously hide individual client updates, tolerate malicious clients, and output calibrated uncertainty for a defined population estimand.
status: Proposed systems-and-statistics target. Secure aggregation can conceal information that robust aggregation would otherwise inspect.
why: It would make private distributed inference resilient to active attacks.
key_works: Kairouz et al., 2021, “Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning,” arXiv:1912.04977; Georgiev and Hopkins, 2022, “Privacy Induces Robustness,” arXiv:2211.00724.

title: Federated multimodal inference without reliable alignment
open: Estimate shared latent structure and its uncertainty when institutions hold different modalities and record alignment is incomplete, private, and error-prone.
status: Proposed target joining federated learning, data integration, and probabilistic linkage. Assuming aligned rows removes a central difficulty.
why: It would enable cross-institution scientific integration without centralizing raw records.
key_works: Lock et al., 2013, “Joint and individual variation explained,” arXiv:1102.4110; Binette and Steorts, 2022, “(Almost) All of Entity Resolution,” arXiv:2008.04443.

title: Hundredfold communication reduction at matched coverage
open: Reduce total transmitted bytes by 100× against a frozen federated-inference baseline while matching centralized confidence-interval coverage and width on prespecified heterogeneous tasks.
status: Proposed moonshot. Communication must include retries, metadata, calibration rounds, and failed runs.
why: It would make uncertainty-aware collaboration feasible on constrained networks.
key_works: Duchi et al., 2014, “Optimality guarantees for distributed statistical estimation,” arXiv:1405.0782; Kairouz et al., 2021, “Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning.”

title: Distinguishing abrupt changes from smooth drift
open: Derive minimax tests and estimators that distinguish jumps from rapidly varying smooth trends under unknown dependence and noise scale.
status: Change-point methods are extensive. A method tuned to piecewise-constant means does not settle discrimination against smooth but steep alternatives.
why: It would reduce false alarms caused by ordinary evolving behavior.
key_works: Truong, Oudre, and Vayatis, 2020, “Selective review of offline change point detection methods,” arXiv:1801.00718, DOI:10.1016/j.sigpro.2019.107299.

title: Change-point intervals after choosing the number of changes
open: Construct simultaneous location intervals that remain valid after data-driven selection of the number, scale, and type of changes under dependent noise.
status: Sharp localization theory exists for important independent mean-change models. Full post-selection coverage is a stronger requirement.
why: It would attach defensible dates to inferred regime changes.
key_works: Wang, Yu, and Rinaldo, 2018/2020, “Univariate Mean Change Point Detection: Penalization, CUSUM and Optimality,” arXiv:1810.09498; Lee et al., 2016, “Exact post-selection inference.”

title: Long-memory testing robust to contamination and breaks
open: Test genuine long-range dependence against short-memory processes with structural breaks or contamination, with sharp separation rates.
status: Proposed research target. Apparent persistence can arise from different mechanisms that standard estimators may conflate.
why: It would improve conclusions about persistence in climate, physiology, and economic data.
key_works: Truong et al., 2020, “Selective review of offline change point detection methods,” arXiv:1801.00718; Hopkins, Li, and Zhang, 2020, “Robust and Heavy-Tailed Mean Estimation Made Simple,” arXiv:2007.15839.

title: Computational limits of covariance change detection
open: Determine statistical and polynomial-time detection boundaries for sparse covariance changes when both the pre-change covariance and change time are unknown.
status: Proposed target connecting high-dimensional change detection and sparse spectral hardness. Mean-change theory alone does not characterize this problem.
why: It would reveal when monitoring altered relationships requires more data than detecting altered averages.
key_works: Berthet and Rigollet, 2013, “Complexity Theoretic Lower Bounds for Sparse Principal Component Detection”; Wang et al., “Univariate Mean Change Point Detection,” arXiv:1810.09498.

title: Forecast uncertainty after repeated backtest tuning
open: Quantify forecast uncertainty after analysts repeatedly choose windows, transformations, models, and evaluation periods using the same time series.
status: Proposed adaptive-inference target. Ordinary backtest intervals typically describe a fixed procedure, not the search that selected it.
why: It would make predictive performance claims less sensitive to retrospective optimization.
key_works: Dwork et al., 2015, “Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis,” arXiv:1411.2664; Zaffran et al., 2022, “Adaptive conformal predictions for time series.”

title: Diffusion inference with uncertain observation mechanisms
open: Estimate drift and diffusion functionals from irregular noisy observations when sampling times are informative and measurement-noise dynamics are unknown but constrained.
status: Nonparametric diffusion inference has a longstanding foundation. Jointly informative observation times and unknown noise create a more difficult inverse problem.
why: It would improve analysis of financial transactions and opportunistic physiological measurements.
key_works: Fan, 2005, “A Selective Overview of Nonparametric Methods in Financial Econometrics,” arXiv:math/0411034, DOI:10.1214/088342305000000412.

title: Minimal-neighborhood Vecchia inference
open: Determine the smallest neighborhood growth needed for asymptotically valid likelihood-based inference under Vecchia approximations across specified covariance families and sampling geometries.
status: Fixed-domain asymptotic results exist under particular conditions. Whether much smaller neighborhoods suffice in broader regimes remains a sharper computational-statistical question.
why: It would justify fast spatial uncertainty estimates rather than only fast predictions.
key_works: Zhang, Tang, and Banerjee, 2024, “Fixed-Domain Asymptotics Under Vecchia’s Approximation of Spatial Process Likelihoods,” DOI:10.5705/ss.202021.0428.

title: Preferential sampling with unknown observation intensity
open: Identify spatial field features and their uncertainty when locations are chosen preferentially and the sampling-intensity model is itself only partially specified.
status: Preferential-sampling models have been studied since at least 2010. Robustness to uncertain selection laws is stronger than fitting one joint parametric model.
why: It would improve inference from monitoring networks concentrated in accessible or high-risk places.
key_works: Diggle, Menezes, and Su, 2010, “Geostatistical inference under preferential sampling,” DOI:10.1111/j.1467-9876.2009.00701.x.

title: Microergodicity in nonstationary anisotropic models
open: Classify which covariance functionals are consistently identifiable under fixed-domain asymptotics for useful nonstationary, anisotropic, and multivariate spatial models.
status: Microergodic parameters are understood in important stationary families. Generalizing the identifiable parameter, rather than assuming all covariance parameters are estimable, remains essential.
why: It would stop spatial models from attaching artificial certainty to nonidentifiable parameters.
key_works: Zhang, Tang, and Banerjee, 2024, “Fixed-Domain Asymptotics Under Vecchia’s Approximation of Spatial Process Likelihoods”; Moraga, 2023, *Spatial Statistics for Data Science: Theory and Practice with R*.

title: Exogenous clustering versus self-excitation
open: Distinguish latent intensity variation from genuine self-excitation in point processes when events are missed, timestamps are imprecise, and observation intensity varies.
status: Proposed identification target. Similar observed clustering can arise from fundamentally different mechanisms.
why: It would improve claims about contagion, aftershocks, and event-triggered behavior.
key_works: Diggle, Menezes, and Su, 2010, “Geostatistical inference under preferential sampling”; Moraga, 2023, *Spatial Statistics for Data Science*.

title: Change-of-support uncertainty
open: Reconstruct fine-scale spatial functionals from heterogeneous area aggregates while providing uncertainty that reflects unresolved within-area variation and changing boundaries.
status: Proposed inverse-inference target. Smooth interpolation does not establish recovery of unobserved local variation.
why: It would improve comparisons across administrative, environmental, and health reporting systems.
key_works: Moraga, 2023, *Spatial Statistics for Data Science: Theory and Practice with R*; World Bank, “Statistical Performance Indicators.”

title: Hundredfold faster calibrated spatial uncertainty
open: Achieve 100× lower end-to-end runtime than a frozen reference method on large spatial datasets while matching predictive and parameter-interval calibration across prespecified misspecification tests.
status: Proposed moonshot. Accuracy must include uncertainty, not only mean prediction or likelihood approximation.
why: It would make uncertainty-aware spatial analysis feasible at operational scale.
key_works: Zhang, Tang, and Banerjee, 2024, “Fixed-Domain Asymptotics Under Vecchia’s Approximation of Spatial Process Likelihoods”; Morris et al., 2019, “Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods.”

title: Honest adaptation across tail classes
open: Characterize when confidence intervals for extreme quantiles can adapt to unknown tail class and second-order bias without losing uniform coverage.
status: Proposed frontier formulation. Adaptation must confront indistinguishability between distributions that agree over observed ranges but differ in remote tails.
why: It would improve the credibility of rare-risk extrapolation.
key_works: Engelke and Ivanovs, 2021, “Sparse Structures for Multivariate Extremes,” arXiv:2004.12182; Bull, 2012, “Honest adaptive confidence bands and self-similar functions.”

title: Graphs mixing asymptotic dependence and independence
open: Build identifiable sparse multivariate tail models that accommodate different pairs or subsets exhibiting asymptotic dependence or asymptotic independence, with valid structure uncertainty.
status: Sparse extremal models are well developed in important regimes. Combining regimes without incoherent joint distributions is a continuing frontier.
why: It would better represent compound risks that do not share one universal tail-dependence pattern.
key_works: Engelke and Ivanovs, 2021, “Sparse Structures for Multivariate Extremes,” arXiv:2004.12182.

title: Joint-tail inference with heterogeneous censoring
open: Estimate multivariate tail probabilities when components have different detection limits, censoring mechanisms, and observation windows, with sharp identifiability and rate results.
status: Proposed target. Treating censored components as missing at random can distort both marginal tails and dependence.
why: It would improve environmental and reliability risk estimates from uneven measurement systems.
key_works: Engelke and Ivanovs, 2021, “Sparse Structures for Multivariate Extremes”; STRATOS Topic Group 8, “Survival Analysis.”

title: Uncertainty decomposition in compound-extreme attribution
open: Quantify how observational error, climate-model discrepancy, causal attribution assumptions, and tail extrapolation jointly affect estimated changes in compound-event risk.
status: Proposed research target. The objective is an explicit uncertainty budget, not a single model-ensemble interval presented as complete.
why: It would improve decisions based on attributed changes in rare-event probabilities.
key_works: Engelke and Ivanovs, 2021, “Sparse Structures for Multivariate Extremes”; Cranmer, Brehmer, and Louppe, 2020, “The frontier of simulation-based inference.”

title: Nonstationary return levels with unknown trend bias
open: Construct return-level intervals that adapt to changing tail parameters while accounting for uncertainty in trend form and extrapolation horizon.
status: Proposed target. Fitting time-varying parameters is not equivalent to establishing valid long-horizon uncertainty under unknown nonstationarity.
why: It would improve infrastructure planning under changing environmental risk.
key_works: Engelke and Ivanovs, 2021, “Sparse Structures for Multivariate Extremes”; Truong et al., 2020, “Selective review of offline change point detection methods.”

title: Hundredfold cheaper certified rare-event estimation
open: Reduce simulator calls by 100× for prespecified rare probabilities while retaining validated relative-error bounds and robustness to importance-sampling model error.
status: Proposed moonshot. The baseline must specify event probabilities, confidence targets, simulator cost, and failure handling.
why: It would make rigorous rare-risk estimates feasible when direct simulation is prohibitive.
key_works: Cranmer, Brehmer, and Louppe, 2020, “The frontier of simulation-based inference”; Morris et al., 2019, “Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods.”

title: Efficient inference in hard stochastic-block-model phases
open: Resolve the polynomial-time detectability frontier in sparse block models with sufficiently many groups where information-theoretic and algorithmic thresholds separate.
status: Thresholds are settled in important two-community and other special regimes. Those successes do not eliminate the harder multi-community phases.
why: It would clarify when network community information is present but computationally inaccessible.
key_works: Abbe, 2017/2018, “Community Detection and Stochastic Block Models: Recent Developments,” arXiv:1703.10146.

title: Graphon uncertainty with nonignorable missing edges
open: Identify graphon functionals and construct confidence sets when dyad observation depends on latent node properties and the unobserved edge value.
status: Proposed target. Standard missing-at-random or fully observed graph assumptions bypass this selection mechanism.
why: It would improve inference from incomplete social, biological, and transaction networks.
key_works: Abbe, “Community Detection and Stochastic Block Models: Recent Developments,” arXiv:1703.10146; Wu, 2022, “Statistical inference with non-probability survey samples.”

title: Graph selection with latent confounders and weak signals
open: Characterize recoverable observed-variable graph structure when hidden factors and sparse direct interactions coexist, including uniformly valid edge uncertainty near weak-signal boundaries.
status: Research target requiring an explicit latent-plus-sparse model. Recovering a covariance matrix does not uniquely resolve causal or conditional graph structure.
why: It would reduce overinterpretation of inferred biological and behavioral networks.
key_works: Loh and Tan, 2015, “High-dimensional robust precision matrix estimation,” arXiv:1509.07229; Mooij and Claassen, 2020, “Constraint-Based Causal Discovery … in the presence of Cycles.”

title: Uncertainty for overlapping multilayer communities
open: Infer the number, overlap, and cross-layer alignment of communities with calibrated uncertainty when layers differ in sparsity and share only some nodes.
status: Proposed target extending block-model and shared-subspace methods. Fixed community count and complete layer alignment are materially easier.
why: It would make multilayer community findings less dependent on arbitrary modeling choices.
key_works: Abbe, “Community Detection and Stochastic Block Models”; Lock et al., 2013, “Joint and individual variation explained,” arXiv:1102.4110.

title: Dynamic networks observed by adaptive queries
open: Derive inference guarantees when edges evolve while an algorithm adaptively chooses which nodes or dyads to inspect under a query budget.
status: Proposed target. Static passive-observation theory does not account for feedback between uncertainty and graph sampling.
why: It would improve active monitoring of expensive or rapidly changing networks.
key_works: Abbe, “Community Detection and Stochastic Block Models,” arXiv:1703.10146; Duchi et al., 2014, “Optimality guarantees for distributed statistical estimation,” arXiv:1405.0782.

title: Goodness-of-fit tests near network criticality
open: Construct calibrated and powerful goodness-of-fit tests for network models near phase transitions, where dependence and parameter uncertainty invalidate simple residual approximations.
status: Proposed testing target. Accurate estimation away from a transition does not establish a uniform null distribution through the critical regime.
why: It would make model criticism possible where network models are most fragile.
key_works: Abbe, “Community Detection and Stochastic Block Models,” arXiv:1703.10146; Wasserman, Ramdas, and Balakrishnan, 2020, “Universal Inference,” arXiv:1912.11436.

title: Identifiable phase–amplitude separation
open: Characterize which constraints allow timing variation and shape variation in random curves to be separately identified, with uncertainty that reflects registration ambiguity.
status: Functional registration is well developed computationally. A unique scientifically meaningful decomposition requires assumptions that need explicit justification.
why: It would improve interpretation of growth curves, movement, and physiological trajectories.
key_works: Morris, 2015, “Functional Regression,” arXiv:1406.4068; Wang, Chiou, and Müller, 2016, “Functional data analysis,” *Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application* 3:257–295.

title: Sparse curves with informative visit times
open: Construct confidence bands and regression inference when each curve is sparsely observed and measurement times depend on its unobserved trajectory.
status: Sparse functional methods exist; informative timing changes the observation model and can bias ordinary smoothing.
why: It would improve longitudinal inference from opportunistic clinical measurements.
key_works: Morris, 2015, “Functional Regression,” arXiv:1406.4068; Diggle, Menezes, and Su, 2010, “Geostatistical inference under preferential sampling.”

title: Functional regression with unknown ill-posedness
open: Obtain honest adaptive inference for functional regression coefficients when predictor covariance eigenvalue decay and coefficient smoothness are both unknown.
status: Estimation and regularization theory provide a baseline. Simultaneous adaptation of uncertainty to unknown ill-posedness is more restrictive.
why: It would make functional regression error bars less dependent on fixed truncation assumptions.
key_works: Morris, 2015, “Functional Regression,” arXiv:1406.4068; Ray, “Adaptive Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise,” arXiv:1407.3397.

title: Fréchet regression through nonunique means
open: Develop inference for metric-space regression when conditional Fréchet means are nonunique or change multiplicity, without arbitrarily selecting one branch.
status: Proposed object-data target. Standard smooth unique-mean asymptotics do not describe transitions between multiple minimizers.
why: It would support uncertainty for shapes, distributions, trees, and other non-Euclidean outcomes.
key_works: Panaretos and Zemel, 2019, “Statistical Aspects of Wasserstein Distances,” arXiv:1806.05500; Wang, Chiou, and Müller, 2016, “Functional data analysis.”

title: Multilevel functional covariance decomposition with missing levels
open: Identify and estimate covariance components when curves are nested or crossed across several levels and some subject–device–occasion combinations are systematically absent.
status: Proposed extension of multilevel functional analysis and data integration. Missing combinations can destroy separability of variance sources.
why: It would improve attribution of variability to people, devices, and environments.
key_works: Morris, 2015, “Functional Regression,” arXiv:1406.4068; Lock et al., 2013, “Joint and individual variation explained.”

title: Minimax conditional-independence testing for functional data
open: Establish sharp testing rates for conditional independence among random functions under explicit spectral and smoothness restrictions, including adaptation to unknown effective dimension.
status: Hilbert-space conditional-independence methods exist. The target is an optimal, adaptive theory rather than unrestricted testing, which faces impossibility.
why: It would strengthen functional graphical models and dynamic biological pathway analysis.
key_works: Shah and Peters, 2020, “The Hardness of Conditional Independence Testing and the Generalised Covariance Measure,” arXiv:1804.07203; Lundborg et al., 2022, Hilbert-space conditional-independence work, DOI:10.1111/rssb.12544.

title: Adaptive Wasserstein confidence sets beyond established regimes
subfield: Optimal transport, topology, and geometric statistics
open: Characterize honest smoothness adaptation for Wasserstein-\(p\) confidence sets beyond the established \(p\leq2\) settings, including unknown support and vanishing densities.
status: Adaptive confidence-set theory already settles important low-dimensional and fixed-support cases. Those results should not be relabeled as open.
why: It would provide uncertainty for distributional comparisons in stronger transport metrics.
key_works: Deo and Randrianarisoa, 2021, “On Adaptive Confidence Sets for the Wasserstein Distances,” arXiv:2111.08505.

title: Confidence sets for transport maps with unknown support
subfield: Optimal transport, topology, and geometric statistics
open: Construct honest uncertainty for optimal transport maps when support geometry, boundary regularity, and density lower bounds are unknown.
status: Transport estimation has a substantial statistical theory. Maps are more sensitive than distances to geometric irregularity and identifiability.
why: It would improve scientific interpretation of distribution-to-distribution correspondences.
key_works: Panaretos and Zemel, 2019, “Statistical Aspects of Wasserstein Distances,” arXiv:1806.05500.

title: Joint statistical–numerical limits for Sinkhorn inference
subfield: Optimal transport, topology, and geometric statistics
open: Derive calibrated inference when sample size, entropic regularization, and numerical stopping tolerance change together, including data-driven regularization selection.
status: Proposed target. Treating the regularization parameter as fixed or the optimization as exact leaves part of the practical error budget unmodeled.
why: It would connect fast transport computation to reliable inferential claims.
key_works: Panaretos and Zemel, 2019, “Statistical Aspects of Wasserstein Distances,” arXiv:1806.05500; Morris et al., 2019, “Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods.”

title: Selective inference for persistent topological features
subfield: Optimal transport, topology, and geometric statistics
open: Assign valid uncertainty to topological features selected after inspecting persistence diagrams, choosing filtrations, and tuning preprocessing.
status: Statistical topological data analysis has established stability and inferential foundations. Adaptive feature selection adds another layer of multiplicity.
why: It would distinguish robust scientific topology from visually selected patterns.
key_works: Wasserman, 2018, “Topological Data Analysis,” arXiv:1609.08227; Lee et al., 2016, “Exact post-selection inference.”

title: Joint uncertainty for topology, dimension, and reach
subfield: Optimal transport, topology, and geometric statistics
open: Determine which sampling and separation conditions permit simultaneous confidence statements for a manifold’s topology, intrinsic dimension, and reach.
status: Proposed geometric-inference target. Estimating one quantity while treating the others as known can conceal circular assumptions.
why: It would make manifold-learning conclusions more scientifically defensible.
key_works: Wasserman, 2018, “Topological Data Analysis,” arXiv:1609.08227; Deo and Randrianarisoa, 2021, “On Adaptive Confidence Sets for the Wasserstein Distances.”

title: SIC measurements in every complex dimension
subfield: Optimal transport, topology, and geometric statistics
open: Prove or disprove that every complex dimension \(d\) admits \(d^2\) equiangular unit vectors defining a symmetric informationally complete quantum measurement.
status: Formulated in the late 1990s; many constructions and numerical solutions exist, but an unconditional all-dimensions theorem remains open in the 2026 problem collection.
why: It would settle the existence of highly symmetric measurement designs for quantum-state estimation.
key_works: Zauner, 1999, doctoral thesis; Zauner, 2011, “Quantum designs: Foundations of a non-commutative design theory”; Bandeira et al., 2026, “Randomstrasse 101: Open Problems of 2025,” arXiv:2603.29571.

title: Adaptive uncertainty with an estimated forward operator
open: Derive minimax confidence sets when a signal and its forward operator are both learned from noisy observations, with adaptation to unknown operator ill-posedness.
status: Linear inverse-problem methods provide important baselines. Treating the operator as fixed can omit the dominant error source.
why: It would improve reconstruction from imperfectly calibrated instruments.
key_works: Spantini et al., 2017, “Goal-oriented optimal approximations of Bayesian linear inverse problems,” arXiv:1607.01881; Ray, “Adaptive Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise.”

title: Bayesian PDE inference near weak identification
open: Establish posterior and frequentist uncertainty guarantees for nonlinear PDE parameters when the observation design makes some directions only weakly identifiable.
status: Proposed target beyond well-conditioned asymptotic regimes. Posterior concentration alone does not guarantee honest uncertainty in weak directions.
why: It would improve trust in inferred material, biological, and environmental parameters.
key_works: Spantini et al., 2017, “Goal-oriented optimal approximations of Bayesian linear inverse problems,” arXiv:1607.01881; Watanabe, 2009, *Algebraic Geometry and Statistical Learning Theory*.

title: Experimental designs that separate calibration and discrepancy
open: Choose physical experiments that maximally separate uncertain model parameters from simulator discrepancy, subject to realistic cost and safety constraints.
status: Proposed design target distinct from the identification question alone. A solution must demonstrate improved recoverability under a stated discrepancy class.
why: It would make expensive simulator-validation campaigns more informative.
key_works: Cranmer, Brehmer, and Louppe, 2020, “The frontier of simulation-based inference”; Wang et al., 2022, “Recent Advances in Bayesian Optimization,” arXiv:2206.03301.

title: Budget-optimal multifidelity uncertainty quantification
open: Allocate computation across simulators of different cost and unknown bias so that the final scientific interval has guaranteed coverage at minimum total expense.
status: Proposed target. Correlation between fidelities is useful, but uncertainty about their discrepancy must also enter the allocation rule.
why: It would reduce simulation cost without disguising approximation error as certainty.
key_works: Wang et al., 2022, “Recent Advances in Bayesian Optimization,” arXiv:2206.03301; Spantini et al., 2017, “Goal-oriented optimal approximations of Bayesian linear inverse problems.”

title: Paley restricted isometry beyond the square-root barrier
open: Prove that explicit Paley-frame constructions satisfy a nontrivial restricted-isometry bound at sparsity growing faster than the square root of the ambient construction size, or disprove the proposed scaling.
status: Explicitly listed in the 2026 Randomstrasse problem collection. Random constructions do not resolve the deterministic arithmetic construction.
why: It would advance deterministic measurement designs for sparse recovery.
key_works: Bandeira et al., 2026, “Randomstrasse 101: Open Problems of 2025,” arXiv:2603.29571; prior Paley-frame work cited therein.
aliases: Paley RIP conjecture; deterministic square-root bottleneck.

title: Blind deconvolution with uncertainty in both factors
open: Determine the statistical–computational frontier for blind deconvolution under explicitly structured signals and kernels, including confidence sets modulo unavoidable scaling and shift symmetries.
status: Proposed inference target. Recovery algorithms under favorable structure do not settle honest uncertainty near ambiguities or nearly nonidentifiable factor pairs.
why: It would improve confidence in reconstructed images, spectra, and instrument responses.
key_works: Spantini et al., 2017, “Goal-oriented optimal approximations of Bayesian linear inverse problems”; Watanabe, 2009, *Algebraic Geometry and Statistical Learning Theory*.

title: Long-horizon sensitivity to informative censoring
open: Construct sharp survival and restricted-mean bounds when censoring depends on unobserved prognosis, with sensitivity parameters that remain interpretable over time.
status: Proposed target within a longstanding survival-analysis challenge. Independent-censoring estimators do not identify outcomes after informative loss to follow-up.
why: It would improve interpretation of long-term treatment and prognosis studies.
key_works: STRATOS Topic Group 8, “Survival Analysis”; Andersen and Keiding, 2002, “Multistate models for event history analysis.”

title: Separable effects under imperfect treatment decomposition
open: Derive sensitivity bounds when the treatment components required to define separable effects cannot be cleanly implemented or may violate their dismissible-component assumptions.
status: Generalized separable-effect theory already includes substantial longitudinal complexity. The remaining target here is robustness to imperfect component interventions.
why: It would clarify whether mechanism-specific treatment effects correspond to feasible interventions.
key_works: Stensrud et al., 2021, “A generalized theory of separable effects in competing event settings,” DOI:10.1007/s10985-021-09530-8.

title: Latent competing-risk times under restricted dependence
open: Determine sharp bounds for latent failure-time functionals under specified dependence restrictions and auxiliary measurements, rather than assuming latent times are fully identifiable.
status: Unrestricted latent competing-risk distributions are not identified from ordinary competing-risk data. The open target is useful restricted identification and inference.
why: It would clarify which hypothetical “failure without competing causes” questions data can support.
key_works: Beyersmann, Allignol, and Schumacher, 2012, *Competing Risks and Multistate Models with R*; Stensrud et al., 2021, “A generalized theory of separable effects.”

title: Multistate models with informative intermittent observation
open: Infer transition intensities and state-occupation probabilities when states are observed intermittently, visit timing depends on hidden state, and recurrent transitions may be missed.
status: Multistate and recurrent-event models provide a foundation. Jointly modeling informative observation and unobserved transitions remains a demanding extension.
why: It would improve analysis of disease progression and repairable systems.
key_works: Andersen and Keiding, 2002, “Multistate models for event history analysis”; Beyersmann et al., 2012, *Competing Risks and Multistate Models with R*.

title: Distinguishing cure from very long latency
open: Design follow-up and auxiliary-measurement strategies that distinguish a genuinely cured subpopulation from a long-tailed failure-time distribution with quantified residual ambiguity.
status: Proposed experimental target. Finite follow-up alone cannot justify arbitrary extrapolation about an event that may occur much later.
why: It would improve interpretation of durable remission and long-term reliability claims.
key_works: STRATOS Topic Group 8, “Survival Analysis”; Engelke and Ivanovs, 2021, “Sparse Structures for Multivariate Extremes.”

title: Dynamic risk calibration under selective follow-up
open: Evaluate and recalibrate time-updated risk predictions when follow-up intensity, treatment, and censoring respond to previous predictions.
status: Proposed target connecting dynamic survival prediction and feedback-aware validation. The evaluation process can change the outcomes being evaluated.
why: It would make deployed prognostic models more accountable.
key_works: STRATOS Topic Group 8, “Survival Analysis”; Barber et al., “Conformal prediction beyond exchangeability,” arXiv:2202.13415.

title: Fine-mapping uncertainty under LD-reference mismatch
subfield: Statistical genetics, omics, and microbiome analysis
open: Construct credible or confidence sets for causal variants that remain calibrated when reference linkage disequilibrium differs from the study population and rare variants are incompletely represented.
status: Statistical fine-mapping is mature, but reference mismatch and unresolved correlated variants remain important limitations.
why: It would improve the reliability of variant prioritization for biological experiments.
key_works: Schaid, Chen, and Larson, 2018, “From genome-wide associations to candidate causal variants by statistical fine-mapping,” DOI:10.1038/s41576-018-0016-z.

title: Cross-population polygenic-score uncertainty
subfield: Statistical genetics, omics, and microbiome analysis
open: Quantify individual and subgroup prediction uncertainty when polygenic scores transfer across populations with different allele frequencies, linkage patterns, environments, and ascertainment.
status: Transferability and unequal predictive performance are documented. The target is calibrated uncertainty and transport diagnostics, not merely improved average accuracy.
why: It would make genetic prediction less likely to amplify unequal evidential support.
key_works: Martin et al., 2019, “Clinical use of current polygenic risk scores may exacerbate health disparities,” DOI:10.1038/s41588-019-0379-x.

title: Gene–environment interaction with inherited confounding
subfield: Statistical genetics, omics, and microbiome analysis
open: Identify gene–environment interactions while separating direct genetic effects, familial environmental transmission, assortative mating, and population structure.
status: Proposed causal-genetic target. Adding principal components does not automatically resolve all familial or environmental pathways.
why: It would improve claims about how environments modify genetic risk.
key_works: Schaid, Chen, and Larson, 2018, “From genome-wide associations to candidate causal variants by statistical fine-mapping”; Cinelli et al., 2025, “A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference.”

title: Uncertainty in unpaired single-cell multiomics alignment
subfield: Statistical genetics, omics, and microbiome analysis
open: Quantify uncertainty in matching cell states across unpaired modalities, including cases with modality-specific populations and nonidentifiable correspondences.
status: Multiomic integration is a recognized single-cell challenge. An attractive joint embedding is not evidence that individual correspondences are identified.
why: It would prevent unsupported mechanistic links between molecular modalities.
key_works: Lähnemann et al., 2020, “Eleven grand challenges in single-cell data science,” DOI:10.1186/s13059-020-1926-6; Lock et al., 2013, “Joint and individual variation explained.”

title: Directional trajectory inference from single-cell snapshots
subfield: Statistical genetics, omics, and microbiome analysis
open: Determine when snapshot molecular measurements identify developmental direction and branching, accounting for uncertain kinetics, cell-cycle effects, and missing lineages.
status: Trajectory inference and dynamics are established challenge areas. The target is identifiable direction with calibrated uncertainty, not only an ordered embedding.
why: It would improve conclusions about differentiation and disease progression.
key_works: Lähnemann et al., 2020, “Eleven grand challenges in single-cell data science,” DOI:10.1186/s13059-020-1926-6.

title: Absolute microbiome abundance under unknown measurement bias
subfield: Statistical genetics, omics, and microbiome analysis
open: Recover absolute abundance changes from compositional sequencing data combined with imperfect spike-ins or total-load measurements, allowing taxon-specific extraction and amplification bias.
status: The compositional nature of microbiome data is established. Absolute inference requires additional measurements and a model for their errors.
why: It would distinguish real biological increases from changes induced by relative normalization.
key_works: Gloor et al., 2017, “Microbiome Datasets Are Compositional: And This Is Not Optional,” DOI:10.3389/fmicb.2017.02224.

title: Measurement invariance with weak external anchors
open: Determine the minimum external calibration needed to distinguish group trait differences from item bias when no item can be assumed perfectly invariant.
status: Proposed identification target. Completely anchor-free separation can be nonidentifiable; the task is sharp inference under explicit weak-anchor information.
why: It would improve fairness and comparability of tests across populations.
key_works: Mair, 2018, *Modern Psychometrics with R*, DOI:10.1007/978-3-319-93177-7.

title: Item-response goodness-of-fit after adaptive testing
open: Develop calibrated model checks when item exposure is chosen adaptively and the fitted trait estimates influence subsequent questions.
status: A 2025 critical review identifies continuing challenges in item-response model assessment. Adaptive exposure changes the reference distribution of diagnostics.
why: It would detect model failures in computerized adaptive tests.
key_works: Sinharay and Monroe, 2025, “Assessment of fit of item response theory models: A critical review of the status quo and some future directions,” DOI:10.1111/bmsp.12378.

title: Separating item drift from population change
open: Estimate time-varying item parameters and population ability distributions when both can change and only a limited set of calibration responses is available.
status: Proposed longitudinal measurement target. Fixing item parameters by assumption can convert item drift into apparent social or educational change.
why: It would improve the interpretation of long-running assessment trends.
key_works: Mair, 2018, *Modern Psychometrics with R*; Sinharay and Monroe, 2025, “Assessment of fit of item response theory models.”

title: Multidimensional traits versus local dependence
open: Characterize when additional latent dimensions can be distinguished from residual dependence among items, with uncertainty about the resulting model structure.
status: Proposed latent-model target. Better likelihood fit from another factor does not uniquely establish another psychological trait.
why: It would improve the scientific interpretation of factor and item-response models.
key_works: Mair, 2018, *Modern Psychometrics with R*; Watanabe, 2009, *Algebraic Geometry and Statistical Learning Theory*.

title: Response shift versus genuine trait change
open: Distinguish changes in a latent trait from changes in how respondents interpret items, especially after treatment, illness, or major life events.
status: Proposed identification and validation target. Longitudinal score changes alone cannot generally separate changed state from changed measurement.
why: It would improve interpretation of patient-reported and psychological outcomes.
key_works: Mair, 2018, *Modern Psychometrics with R*; QIBA Technical Performance Working Group, 2015, “Quantitative Imaging Biomarkers: A Review of Statistical Methods for Technical Performance Assessment.”

title: Measuring ability under AI-assisted responding
open: Build randomized validation datasets distinguishing unaided ability, effective tool use, and answer substitution when respondents have access to AI assistance.
status: Proposed experimental target. Success requires external criterion tasks, documented assistance conditions, and longitudinal transfer tests rather than only detecting AI-written answers.
why: It would clarify what modern assessments actually measure.
key_works: Sinharay and Monroe, 2025, “Assessment of fit of item response theory models,” DOI:10.1111/bmsp.12378; Mair, 2018, *Modern Psychometrics with R*.

title: Joint identification of publication bias and analytic selection
open: Separate publication selection, within-study specification search, and genuine effect heterogeneity using published summaries plus limited audit or registry data.
status: Publication-bias identification methods exist under explicit assumptions. Adding unobserved analytic selection creates a distinct identification problem.
why: It would improve the credibility of evidence synthesis.
key_works: Andrews and Kasy, 2019, “Identification of and Correction for Publication Bias,” DOI:10.1257/aer.20180310; Botvinik-Nezer et al., 2020, “Variability in the analysis of a single neuroimaging dataset by many teams.”

title: Meta-analysis with unknown study overlap
open: Construct valid pooled estimates when studies share participants or source databases but overlap and induced covariance are only partially known.
status: Proposed target. Treating overlapping estimates as independent can create fictitious precision; complete individual-level deduplication is often unavailable.
why: It would improve synthesis of administrative, genetic, and platform-based research.
key_works: Binette and Steorts, 2022, “(Almost) All of Entity Resolution,” arXiv:2008.04443; Andrews and Kasy, 2019, “Identification of and Correction for Publication Bias.”

title: A generalizable distribution of analyst uncertainty
open: Estimate how conclusions vary across a target population of competent analysts and defensible pipelines, rather than only among volunteers in one many-analyst study.
status: Many-team experiments demonstrate analytic variability. Generalizing that variability requires an explicit analyst and task sampling design.
why: It would make analytic flexibility a measurable uncertainty component.
key_works: Botvinik-Nezer et al., 2020, “Variability in the analysis of a single neuroimaging dataset by many teams,” DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-2314-9.

title: Replication failure versus population transport failure
open: Design replication programs that distinguish an unstable original finding from a genuinely population-specific effect or a changed intervention.
status: Proposed experimental target. A different result in a new setting is not, by itself, enough to identify which explanation is responsible.
why: It would make replication evidence more diagnostically useful.
key_works: Tipton and Olsen, 2018, “A Review of Statistical Methods for Generalizing From Evaluations of Educational Interventions”; Cinelli et al., 2025, “A Dozen Challenges in Causality and Causal Inference.”

title: Living meta-analysis with overlapping sequential evidence
open: Update evidence continuously while controlling error despite repeated looks, selective arrival of studies, participant overlap, and revisions to earlier results.
status: Proposed synthesis target joining sequential inference and publication-selection models. Simply rerunning a conventional meta-analysis after every study is insufficient.
why: It would make continuously maintained evidence summaries statistically defensible.
key_works: Ramdas et al., 2023, “Game-Theoretic Statistics and Safe Anytime-Valid Inference,” arXiv:2210.01948; Andrews and Kasy, 2019, “Identification of and Correction for Publication Bias.”

title: Optimal allocation of replication budgets
open: Allocate a fixed replication budget across claims to maximize decision-relevant information while accounting for selection bias, heterogeneous costs, and correlated hypotheses.
status: Proposed decision problem. Ranking studies by significance or citation count is not an established optimum for scientific value.
why: It would make limited replication funding more effective.
key_works: Andrews and Kasy, 2019, “Identification of and Correction for Publication Bias”; Wang et al., 2022, “Recent Advances in Bayesian Optimization,” arXiv:2206.03301.

title: Transporting accelerated-life tests across failure mechanisms
open: Determine when accelerated testing preserves the failure mechanism relevant to ordinary use, and construct uncertainty bounds when mechanism switching is possible.
status: Reliability methods are extensive; modern heterogeneous usage creates additional transport and model-validation challenges.
why: It would prevent accelerated tests from giving precise answers about the wrong failure process.
key_works: Meeker and Hong, 2014, “Reliability Meets Big Data: Opportunities and Challenges,” DOI:10.1080/08982112.2014.846119; Hong, Zhang, and Meeker, 2018, “Big Data and Reliability Applications: The Complexity Dimension,” arXiv:1803.06206.

title: Counterfactual failure risk under preventive maintenance
open: Estimate failure distributions under alternative maintenance policies when maintenance is triggered by latent degradation and prevents observation of the failures it would avert.
status: Proposed causal-reliability target. Ordinary censoring assumptions can fail because maintenance decisions are informative.
why: It would improve maintenance policy evaluation without waiting for avoidable failures.
key_works: Hong, Zhang, and Meeker, 2018, “Big Data and Reliability Applications: The Complexity Dimension,” arXiv:1803.06206; Stensrud et al., 2021, “A generalized theory of separable effects.”

title: Rare-failure transfer across heterogeneous fleets
open: Borrow reliability information across product generations and operating environments while giving valid uncertainty for new or sparsely observed fleets.
status: Heterogeneous reliability data are a documented challenge. The target is guarded transfer, not unqualified pooling.
why: It would enable earlier reliability assessment without concealing fleet-specific risks.
key_works: Hong, Zhang, and Meeker, 2018, “Big Data and Reliability Applications: The Complexity Dimension,” DOI:10.1080/00224065.2018.1438007.

title: Compression preserving remaining-life uncertainty
open: Design sensor compression that preserves specified remaining-useful-life probabilities and interval calibration, including uncertainty introduced by discarded high-frequency information.
status: Proposed engineering target. Preserving average prediction error is weaker than preserving failure-tail inference.
why: It would reduce telemetry cost without undermining safety-relevant predictions.
key_works: Meeker and Hong, 2014, “Reliability Meets Big Data: Opportunities and Challenges”; Duchi et al., 2014, “Optimality guarantees for distributed statistical estimation.”

title: Validating nondestructive failure surrogates
open: Collect paired nondestructive measurements and eventual failure outcomes across operating conditions to test whether surrogate degradation signals remain predictive near rare failure modes.
status: Proposed experimental target. Correlation during ordinary operation does not establish sensitivity to every consequential failure mechanism.
why: It would make low-cost monitoring a credible substitute for destructive testing.
key_works: Meeker and Hong, 2014, “Reliability Meets Big Data: Opportunities and Challenges”; QIBA Technical Performance Working Group, 2015, “Quantitative Imaging Biomarkers: A Review of Statistical Methods for Technical Performance Assessment.”

title: Tenfold cheaper physical reliability qualification
open: Reduce physical test expenditure by at least 10× while matching preregistered reliability bounds and out-of-condition validation performance, using justified simulation and accelerated testing.
status: Proposed moonshot. Savings must include simulator development, calibration specimens, and the cost of failed qualification attempts.
why: It would accelerate product development without weakening reliability evidence.
key_works: Hong, Zhang, and Meeker, 2018, “Big Data and Reliability Applications: The Complexity Dimension”; Cranmer et al., 2020, “The frontier of simulation-based inference.”

title: Hadamard matrices of every admissible order
open: Prove or disprove that a Hadamard matrix exists for every positive order divisible by four.
status: A classical unresolved existence conjecture with many infinite constructions and extensive computational progress. Historical lists of the smallest missing orders should not be treated as current records.
why: It would complete a basic existence foundation for orthogonal two-level designs and coding constructions.
key_works: Hadamard, 1893, determinant work; “Quaternionic Perfect Sequences and Hadamard Matrices,” 2026, arXiv:2601.22337; OEIS A007299 for evolving existence records.

title: Nonexistence of larger circulant Hadamard matrices
open: Prove or disprove that the only nontrivial circulant Hadamard matrices have order four.
status: A longstanding conjecture. Strong arithmetic restrictions exclude many possible orders but do not constitute an all-orders proof.
why: It would settle a highly structured class of orthogonal sequence designs.
key_works: Leung and Schmidt, 2012, “New restrictions on possible orders of circulant Hadamard matrices,” DOI:10.1007/s10623-011-9493-1; “Quaternionic Perfect Sequences and Hadamard Matrices,” 2026, arXiv:2601.22337.
aliases: Circulant Hadamard conjecture; Ryser’s circulant Hadamard conjecture.

title: Barker sequences longer than thirteen
open: Prove that no binary Barker sequence has length greater than thirteen, or construct one.
status: Odd lengths beyond thirteen are excluded; the unresolved even-length case is connected to circulant Hadamard matrices. Large numerical exclusions do not settle all lengths.
why: It would resolve an extremal low-autocorrelation design problem.
key_works: Turyn and Storer, 1961, “On binary sequences”; Leung and Schmidt, 2005, “The field descent method”; Leung and Schmidt, 2012, “New restrictions on possible orders of circulant Hadamard matrices.”

title: Three mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order ten
open: Construct three pairwise mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order ten, or prove that no such triple exists.
status: A specific longstanding design problem. Recent SAT work resolves restricted structural cases, not the unrestricted triple-existence question.
why: It would advance exact small-design existence and constraint-solving methods.
key_works: Myrvold, 1999, “Negative results for orthogonal triples of Latin squares of order 10”; Bright, Keita, and Stevens, 2026, “Myrvold’s results on orthogonal triples of 10×10 Latin squares: A SAT investigation,” DOI:10.37236/13960; “Improving SAT Solvers on Orthogonal Latin Square Problems,” 2026, arXiv:2605.02132.

title: Projective plane of order twelve
open: Determine whether a finite projective plane of order twelve exists; equivalently, whether a symmetric \(2\!-\!(157,13,1)\) design exists.
status: A classical unresolved finite-geometry existence problem. Necessary arithmetic conditions do not rule out order twelve.
why: It would clarify the limits of highly balanced incidence designs.
key_works: Elkies, 2015, Harvard Math 155 finite-geometry notes; classical projective-plane and balanced-design literature.

title: Full transversals in odd-order Latin squares
open: Prove or disprove that every Latin square of odd order has a transversal containing one cell from every row, every column, and every symbol.
status: A longstanding full-transversal conjecture. Results about near-transversals do not settle the full odd-order statement.
why: It would strengthen existence guarantees for balanced selections in combinatorial designs.
key_works: Ryser, 1967, formulation; Wanless, 2011, “Transversals in Latin squares: a survey” (verify bibliographic details); Wanless, “Data on transversals in Latin squares.”

title: Machine-readable statistical assumptions
subfield: Statistical software, benchmarks, and research infrastructure
open: Build an interoperable format linking estimands, assumptions, diagnostics, algorithms, and guarantees, with executable checks for the assumptions that are empirically testable.
status: Proposed infrastructure target. Metadata standards exist, but a dataset’s accessibility does not encode the conditions needed for a particular inferential claim.
why: It would make statistical analyses easier to audit and compose.
key_works: Wilkinson et al., 2016, “The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship,” DOI:10.1038/sdata.2016.18; Gelman et al., 2020, “Bayesian Workflow.”

title: Hidden-truth benchmarks for statistical robustness
subfield: Statistical software, benchmarks, and research infrastructure
open: Create benchmark families with withheld generating mechanisms, realistic shifts, contamination, and ground-truth estimands, preventing method developers from tuning directly to every evaluation case.
status: Proposed data target. Simulation-study design principles exist; the contribution is a governed, versioned benchmark that measures generalization of statistical guarantees.
why: It would expose methods that work only on their authors’ preferred simulations.
key_works: Morris, White, and Crowther, 2019, “Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods,” DOI:10.1002/sim.8086; Lueckmann et al., 2021, “Benchmarking Simulation-Based Inference.”

title: Numerical coverage audits across hardware
subfield: Statistical software, benchmarks, and research infrastructure
open: Measure and explain changes in confidence coverage, posterior tails, and test size caused by floating-point precision, GPU kernels, parallel reductions, and numerical libraries.
status: Proposed empirical infrastructure target. Numerical agreement of point estimates is not sufficient evidence of inferential equivalence.
why: It would identify when hardware acceleration changes scientific conclusions.
key_works: Morris et al., 2019, “Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods”; Vehtari et al., 2021, “Rank-normalization, folding, and localization.”

title: Cross-language probabilistic reproducibility
subfield: Statistical software, benchmarks, and research infrastructure
open: Specify and test equivalent sampling, missing-value, weighting, and likelihood semantics across major statistical languages, separating intended randomness from implementation discrepancies.
status: Proposed engineering target. Reproducing a seed within one implementation does not ensure equivalent statistical computation elsewhere.
why: It would reduce silent discrepancies when analyses are ported or independently replicated.
key_works: Wilkinson et al., 2016, “The FAIR Guiding Principles”; Gelman et al., 2020, “Bayesian Workflow,” arXiv:2011.01808.

title: Hundredfold faster resampling of adaptive pipelines
subfield: Statistical software, benchmarks, and research infrastructure
open: Reduce end-to-end bootstrap or randomization-inference cost by 100× while preserving interval calibration for pipelines that include model selection, preprocessing, and refitting.
status: Proposed moonshot. Reusing only a final fitted model is not equivalent to resampling the procedure that selected it.
why: It would make realistic uncertainty accounting affordable.
key_works: Bengio and Grandvalet, 2004, “No Unbiased Estimator of the Variance of K-Fold Cross-Validation”; Lee et al., 2016, “Exact post-selection inference”; Morris et al., 2019, “Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods.”

title: Verified counterexample discovery for statistical claims
subfield: Statistical software, benchmarks, and research infrastructure
open: Build tools that search for distributions violating a claimed statistical guarantee and produce independently checkable witnesses, while respecting the claim’s exact assumptions.
status: Proposed engineering target. An adversarial simulation is useful evidence, but a verified counterexample requires controlling numerical error and assumption membership.
why: It would accelerate correction of false or overgeneralized statistical results.
key_works: Buhai et al., 2025, “The Quasi-Polynomial Low-Degree Conjecture is False,” arXiv:2505.17360; Morris et al., 2019, “Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods.”

title: Sustainable financing for longitudinal statistical systems
open: Design and evaluate multiyear financing arrangements that preserve survey continuity, sampling quality, revision transparency, and independent publication through funding shocks.
status: Proposed funding target. Success should be measured by continuity and statistical quality, not merely money committed or surveys announced.
why: It would protect the time series on which public and scientific decisions depend.
key_works: PARIS21, statistical-capacity development programme; World Bank, “Statistical Performance Indicators” framework.

title: Financing representative cohorts without extractive data collection
open: Establish durable funding and governance for underrepresented cohorts, with community control, retained local capacity, and prespecified improvements in inferential coverage.
status: Proposed funding target. Increasing sample counts alone does not guarantee representation, transportability, or equitable data stewardship.
why: It would improve both scientific validity and the distribution of research benefits.
key_works: Martin et al., 2019, “Clinical use of current polygenic risk scores may exacerbate health disparities”; PARIS21, statistical-capacity development programme.

title: Maintenance funding for foundational statistical software
open: Develop a sustainable funding model for statistical libraries that rewards correctness, dependency maintenance, documentation, and long-term compatibility rather than only new features or papers.
status: Proposed funding and evaluation target. Required outcomes should include audited defects, maintenance response times, and reproducible releases.
why: It would protect widely reused inference from infrastructure neglect.
key_works: Wilkinson et al., 2016, “The FAIR Guiding Principles”; He, Madigan, Yu, and Wellner, 2025, “Statistics at a Crossroads; Who is for the Challenge?” arXiv:2503.22945.

title: Reproducible cross-jurisdiction secure-data research
open: Create governance and funding arrangements under which analyses can be independently reproduced across secure data environments without transferring prohibited raw records.
status: Proposed institutional target. Technical federation alone does not resolve access review, incompatible permissions, disclosure rules, or reproducibility obligations.
why: It would unlock verifiable research across institutions and national boundaries.
key_works: Kairouz et al., 2021, “Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning,” arXiv:1912.04977; Wilkinson et al., 2016, “The FAIR Guiding Principles.”

title: Independent validation of census and vital-registration coverage
open: Fund recurring independent validation studies that estimate undercount, duplicate registration, linkage error, and uncertainty in civil-registration and census systems.
status: Proposed funding target grounded in statistical-capacity needs. Success requires published error estimates and improvement tracking, not just administrative digitization.
why: It would improve denominators and population facts used throughout public policy.
key_works: World Bank, “Statistical Performance Indicators”; PARIS21, statistical-capacity development programme; U.S. Census Bureau, “Data Linkage Infrastructure.”

title: Funded publication of null results and replication evidence
open: Test funding and publication mechanisms that make preregistered null results, failed replications, and negative methodological findings reliably discoverable and reusable.
status: Proposed policy experiment. Its success criterion is measured reduction in selective evidence availability, not the creation of another optional registry.
why: It would improve the evidence base on which subsequent inference depends.
key_works: Andrews and Kasy, 2019, “Identification of and Correction for Publication Bias,” DOI:10.1257/aer.20180310; Wilkinson et al., 2016, “The FAIR Guiding Principles.”
